jobs.title: Director of Product: Capital One Shopping (Remote - Eligible)
jobs.desc:
Director of Product: Capital One Shopping (Remote - Eligible)

Come join our growing team in Capital One Shopping - If you have a remarkable ability to use data to tell a story, form a hypothesis and define metrics to identify the success of product initiatives - this is the role for you!

Product Management at Capital One is a booming, vibrant craft that requires reimagining the status quo, finding value creation opportunities, and driving innovative and sustainable customer experiences through technology. We believe our portfolio of businesses and investments in growth and transformation will result in a company with the scale, brand, capabilities, talent, and values to succeed as the digital revolution transforms our society and our industry.

We're looking for a Director of Product Management with a demonstrated interest and aptitude for AI. While formal on-the-job experience with AI is a plus, we highly value candidates who have proactively incorporated AI into their personal projects, explored AI-driven development environments (e.g., Cursor, GitHub Copilot), or built automations using AI agents. Show us how you've used AI to learn, build, and solve problems beyond basic text generation.

Capital One Product Framework

In this role, you'll be expected to demonstrate proficiency in five key areas which we consider to be the foundation for successful Product management:

  • Human Centered - Obsesses about internal and external customer needs to reimagine and innovate product solutions
  • Business Focused - Delivers game-changing outcomes by focusing on leverage and execution excellence
  • Technology Driven - Leverages technology to deliver innovative and resilient solutions that enable both near term and long term value
  • Integrated Problem Solving - Identifies and resolves complex problems to deliver outcomes while mitigating product risks
  • Transformational Leadership - Leads cross functional teams to solve customer problems and drive organizational alignment


What we are looking for:
  • A knowledge and passion for emerging technologies (API's, Big Data, Native UI's) to incorporate into building great products
  • Use SQL to build a data-back strategy, identify insights, and troubleshoot issues
  • Own day to day setting and monitoring of KPIs - requires strong SQL/data analysis skills
  • Someone comfortable with backend products who is not afraid to challenge the norm and do what is right for the team
  • Proficiency in handling large data files using SQL, Python, and/or R
  • Own day to day operations of product, including identifying bugs or leverage opportunities via comprehensive understanding of data
  • A product centric mindset to take a product from ideation to production and continually iterate improvements
  • A customer-first mindset
  • A strategic thought leader who can create a compelling vision and story to present to senior executives and inspire direct and partner teams

  • Partner deeply with CX Operations to build agent tooling that makes human agents dramatically more effective — AI copilot, full journey context, auto-generated summaries.

Agencies, in-house media buying teams, and enterprise buyers managing 10+ ad accounts and launching 50+ ads a week use Koast to launch faster, automate optimizations off real attribution data, and see every account from one hub. The Koast Agent is the next layer: an AI that reads the account, spots what matters, and acts inside guardrails.

We are a small team shipping fast. The product is live, customers are paying, a Whop partnership just onboarded a wave of new users, and the Agent build is underway. What we do not have is one person who owns the product end to end: what gets built, why, in what order, and whether it actually landed.

That is this role. It starts at 20 hours a week on contract. If you are the right person, it becomes the full-time product seat at Koast.

What you will own

Discovery that finds the real problem. You will sit in on enterprise sales calls and onboarding sessions, run discovery with agencies and media buying teams, and figure out what they are actually trying to get done versus what they say they want. Every feature request gets mapped to a job: launching smoother, getting their team in, getting tasks done, keeping users active and growing spend inside Koast. If it does not serve a job, it does not get built.

Specs that engineering can execute without a meeting. We run a lean engineering team plus an AI-assisted dev pipeline. That only works when the ticket is unambiguous. You will write PRDs and Shortcut tickets that define the behavior, the edge cases, the data dependencies (Meta API limits, Hyros and Cometly attribution feeds, Whop account provisioning), and the acceptance criteria. If an engineer or an agent has to guess, the spec was not done.

The queue, and what is missing from it. You own the Up Next column. You will keep engineering fed so they are never blocked, and you will keep a standing view of what is discussed in Slack, support, and QA that does not yet have a ticket. Gaps are your problem before they become customer problems.

Evidence over opinion. PostHog, Intercom, session replays, rage clicks, support threads. You will run the user-behavior audit, know where people drop off in launching, and bring numbers to every prioritization argument, including the ones with the CEO.

Delivery from spec to shipped. Governance, milestones, release notes, and the customer conversation after it ships. When something breaks or slips, you are the one who says so early, not the one who explains it after.

Technical judgement in a non-deterministic product. The Koast Agent makes decisions off data that is noisy, seasonal, and shaped by Meta's learning phase. You will make product calls that respect that: what the Agent is allowed to do, what it must never do, how we measure whether an automated action was correct. Guardrails are infrastructure here, not UI. You need to understand why.

What you will do week to week

  • Run discovery sessions with prospects and customers and turn them into scoped, execution-ready PRDs.
  • Surface technical risk early: undocumented API behavior, missing data, an assumption that will not survive a real ad account.
  • Write and groom Shortcut tickets with enough detail for an engineer or Claude Code to ship without a follow-up question.
  • Partner with engineering on feasibility, sequencing, and cutting scope to what ships this week.

**About us**
------------

Recidiviz is creating safer, healthier communities by improving outcomes for people in the criminal justice system. We build technology to reduce the number of people in prison and to help criminal justice leaders embrace data-driven decision-making.

Using software tools and thoughtful product design, we've been able to safely reduce incarceration and improve outcomes. We work side-by-side with leaders of the criminal justice system, people in prison and on supervision, and ecosystem partners to build a better path forward. In addition to the revenue we earn from state partners, some of the most respected philanthropists and foundations support our work.

People who succeed at Recidiviz lead with kindness and humility, assume good intent, learn from failure, and fix problems when they see them. They are excited to work arm in arm with government leadership and staff to improve outcomes. They are great listeners. They build deep relationships with and empathy for the people we work with and the people who our mission serves, even when those two groups feel at odds.

Your job is to make each of them sharper, more supported, and more impactful: setting strategic context, building the people systems that help them grow, and creating the conditions for them to build products that actually get used on a daily and weekly basis. You'll report to the Chief Impact Officer and serve as a key partner on product direction, team health, operational standards, and organizational strategy as Recidiviz scales nationally. Some travel to our state partners, internal team gatherings, and offsites is expected.

This role owns customer and business outcomes, transforming validated market and user needs into differentiated, scalable capabilities that reinforce a coherent and integrated Orion experience.

Working closely with a peer senior product leader, engineering, data science, customer-facing teams, and executive leadership, the Senior Director ensures cross-functional alignment and drives continuous improvement. This is a hands-on leadership role, setting vision and priorities for a defined Orion domain and directly leading discovery, prioritization, and execution with Precision eControl and Vorys eControl stakeholders. ***At this time, candidates who would work in the following states will not be considered for this role: VT, RI, NY, NJ, NH, MI, ME, MA, DE, CO, CT, CA, and AZ.***

* **Product development and outcome delivery:** Guide the full product lifecycle for pillar capabilities. Lead cross-functional teams from discovery through delivery, launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration. Develop solutions that are valuable, feasible, usable, viable, and scalable.

* **Go-to-market and organizational enablement:** Work with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Vorys eControl, and other stakeholders to shape positioning, launch readiness, enablement, customer communication, and feedback loops for the assigned domain.
* **Product leadership and talent development:** Coach and develop product manager(s), establish clear decision context and accountability, strengthen product craft, and model rigorous, customer-centered, outcome-oriented product leadership across Precision eControl.

* The portfolio is multiplying. We are moving from one product line to a platform spanning sales, service, data, F&I, payments and digital retail. Each department has a different buyer, a different competitor set and a different vocabulary. Nobody owns the messaging architecture that ties them together.

* Product velocity is ahead of field readiness. Engineering and product are shipping at a pace the company has never operated at. Sales, account management, onboarding and support need enablement that is timely, credible and actually used, and we do not yet have the system to produce it.

* The category is up for grabs. The market wants to put us in the CRM box. Our thesis is that AI agents change what "CRM" means, and the company that explains that best to a skeptical, relationship-driven buyer wins the next decade of auto retail software. That story needs an owner.

Engineering ships with AI, our internal agents answer the field's questions, and every function is expected to automate its own work. Product marketing has to be built that way from day one, which is why the person who builds it matters so much.

Lead the multi-year narrative evolution from CRM to AI Engagement Platform, and make it land with three very different audiences: the owner-operator of one store, the centralized buying group running 5 to 15 rooftops, and the enterprise group with a CFO in the room.  
  
**Launches**. Design and run our new product introduction system: launch tiers, the artifacts each tier gets, who does what, and how we measure whether the launch worked. Build it AI-first, so that a monthly agent cadence produces a full set of launch assets without a monthly scramble. Then run the big ones yourself. NADA Show (February, Orlando) is the industry's Dreamforce and our largest launch moment of the year; you will own the product marketing plan for it.

**Director, Product Management (PrintOps)**  
**Pharos | US Remote**

  
  
*Here's what you'd actually be stepping into: an established product, two new markets it hasn't reached yet, and no one left who can tell you why it behaves the way it does. Some people need that explanation handed to them. Others go dig it up themselves. This role is for the second kind.*

### About Pharos

Pharos Systems International is the leader in PrintOps, the integrated, user-centric, and cloud-native approach to managing printing and the infrastructure and operations behind it. Pharos' modern print management software empowers enterprises to reduce costs, strengthen security, and support today's hybrid workforce with simple, reliable, and scalable printing solutions. Trusted by thousands of organizations, including many of the world's largest Fortune 500 companies, Pharos has helped eliminate print servers, cut millions in print-related spend, and accelerate the transition to cloud-based infrastructure. Headquartered in Rochester, NY, Pharos has been delivering innovative print management solutions and measurable ROI since 1992.  
  
Our flagship product already runs inside a large, established customer base, which means it carries real history, real workarounds, and a level of hidden complexity that isn't written down anywhere. We're also pushing it into new markets it hasn't served before, without losing the trust of the customers who already rely on it every day. That combination, protecting what works while extending what's possible, is exactly why this role exists.

### What This Role Is

jobs.desc:
**Director, Product Management (Security)**  
**Pharos | US Remote**

  
  
*Here's what you'd actually be walking into: one early customer, a real thesis, and everything else still unproven. Some people need the market validated before they'll commit to building in it. Others want to be the one who proves it's real. This role is for the second kind.*

### About Pharos

Pharos Systems International is the leader in PrintOps, the integrated, user-centric, and cloud-native approach to managing printing and the infrastructure and operations behind it. Pharos' modern print management software empowers enterprises to reduce costs, strengthen security, and support today's hybrid workforce with simple, reliable, and scalable printing solutions. Trusted by thousands of organizations, including many of the world's largest Fortune 500 companies, Pharos has helped eliminate print servers, cut millions in print-related spend, and accelerate the transition to cloud-based infrastructure. Headquartered in Rochester, NY, Pharos has been delivering innovative print management solutions and measurable ROI since 1992.  
  
Pharos has an early proof of concept in security and real conviction about where the market is headed. What we don't have yet is proof it holds up at scale, or a repeatable way to turn that thesis into a validated business. That gap is exactly why this role exists.

### What This Role Is

This role owns the full loop from thesis to revenue: understanding who the real buyer is and what they'll actually pay to solve, turning an existing proof of concept into something multiple customers can rely on, and building the go-to-market motion that gets it from a handful of pilots to a repeatable business.  
  
You'll work directly with Engineering, not just direct it: prototyping, reviewing technical tradeoffs, and getting into implementation details yourself when that's the fastest way to learn something. You'll also work directly with customers and, over time, with Sales, to turn early proof into paying accounts.  
  
You'll report directly to the CEO, with the autonomy that comes with that and the visibility too. There's no team here yet. What you build, you build largely with your own judgment and your own hands.

### What You Will Own

* The market thesis: who the real buyer is, what they're actually willing to pay for, and what this product will deliberately not attempt.
* The path from an early proof of concept to something multiple paying customers can rely on.
* Direct, hands-on work with Engineering: epics, prototypes, requirements, and implementation tradeoffs.
* The go-to-market motion: positioning, packaging, pricing input, and what it takes to turn a pilot into a paying customer.
* A fast, honest read on what's working and what isn't, reported straight to the CEO, without waiting for a perfect plan to have that conversation.

### What a Strong Background Looks Like

* You've built and shipped something close to zero to one, not just contributed to an already-mature product line.
* You've worked directly with customers to test whether a problem is real and worth paying to solve, not just gathered requirements secondhand.
* You've gotten into the technical details yourself: a prototype, a proof of concept, a spec you wrote and then helped build.
* You've made a real call with incomplete information and lived with the outcome, good or bad.
* You reach for AI as a normal part of how you think through a problem, not as a novelty.

**Not a good fit if…**

**Strong fit if…**

  

You need a validated market and an established team in place before you're willing to commit to a direction.

You're comfortable being the person who validates the market, not just executing inside one someone else already proved.

  

Your best work has come from directing others rather than building things yourself.

You still want to be hands-on with prototypes and implementation, not just strategy.

As a Director of Product at SureCost, you'll own the business of a set of products that pharmacies

environment.

show what changed because of your decisions.

jobs.desc:
We are looking for a Director, Product Management – Job Ingestion to own and drive our enterprise job acquisition and processing strategy. You will serve as the strategic product leader bridging technical data systems with core business growth levers.

In this role, you will lead the evolution of our web scraping, API feed integrations, ATS (Applicant Tracking System) connections, real-time event processing, and job parsing/normalization architectures across all BOLD web properties. The ideal candidate does not require domain experience in recruitment technology or HR tech, but must bring a strong background in data engineering or data systems (e.g., former Data Engineer, Systems Architect, or Technical Data PM).

This is a player/coach role and you should be skilled at driving outcomes as an individual contributor at times. You will leverage your technical depth to partner credibly with principal data engineers while applying strong business judgment and executive storytelling to connect job inventory health, latency, and quality directly to platform engagement, SEO footprint, and monetization.

**About this team**

Job Ingestion is the foundational engine that powers BOLD's entire job discovery and recruitment platform. jobs.desc:
**Type::** Full-time

**Location:** Remote, with a preference for candidates located in NY, TX, MD, or GA

**Compensation:** $140,000 - $180,000

**Job Level:** Director/VP (depending on experience)

**ABOUT LEMONTREE**
-------------------

There are more food pantries in the US than there are McDonalds, but most families facing hunger don't take that help. That's why we started Lemontree–because it makes no sense for our neighbors to go hungry when there's free food around the corner. We've helped one million households access the free food in their communities by bringing technology + empathy to the experience of food assistance. Learn more about us at https://www.foodhelpline.org/about.

### **Our Values**

**Service Over Self**

We put the mission — helping people find food — ahead of ego, credit, or agenda. That means caring for the people we serve and the team around us, and going the extra mile when it makes a real difference. We're here for the work itself and what it makes possible for others.

**Ownership**

We get shit done and we carry our piece so the whole team can move forward. When we make a mistake, we name it early and openly, because a problem we've owned out loud is one we can fix together. In a growing org, this kind of autonomy & accountability is how we do big things with a small team.

**Curiosity**  
We don't take anything for granted. We stay curious about our users and ourselves. We stay humble enough to accept that there's always room to improve. We stay ready to change course when the evidence points somewhere new. The plan we have today is a strong draft, but we'll always need to adapt to a changing world. We'd rather ask the better question and adjust than defend a stale answer.

**THE POSITION**
----------------

Lemontree is looking for a **Head of Product** **& Technology** that will partner with the Executive Director to own and evolve our platform strategy to scale our impact. Since 2020, we've grown from a simple helpline into a platform that serves thousands of families, partners, and volunteers daily. What we need now is someone who can shepherd us to the next level, bringing rigor and direction to how we evolve: sharper prioritization, better use of our data, and clearer decision-making & process around where we invest our resources. Every decision we make should align with our strategic anchors:

* User-centered

* Hospitality in every interaction

* Built for scale

This is a hands-on leadership role with high trust and high agency, reporting to the Executive Director. You'll be the person setting product direction and leading the charge to move it forward, partnering with an engineering agency on execution and collaborating closely across our broader Lemontree team. While product ownership is the focus, this is a multi-disciplinary position that combines product management, data analysis, and technical leadership to build toward stability *and* scalability. If you like operating with real autonomy and are motivated to take things from 1 100, this role will suit you.

### **What You'll Do**

Drive **technical leadership** that delivers a reliable, joyful, scalable user experience for neighbors looking for food assistance.

* Serve as a credible technical voice in conversations about architecture, tradeoffs, and feasibility.
* Direct our engineering agency, translating product priorities into well-scoped technical work and holding a high bar for what ships.
* Oversee third party services that support our product, including setting up integrations, managing billing, negotiating nonprofit discounts, etc.

Own a **product roadmap** that increases the breadth & depth of our impact, aligned with our organizational strategy.

* Partner with CEO & senior leadership to shape overall strategy & product direction. Rather than making every single product decision, you will own the process that helps those decisions happen with the right information, clear accountability, and strong follow-through.

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Atlassian is reimagining the future of teamwork with AI at its core. Jira’s mission is to autonomously organize, plan, and track work for our customers, then supply context from Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph to agents that help get the work done.

We’re looking for a visionary **Head of Product for Jira** to lead the product organization responsible for Jira’s experience, AI, and customer adoption. In this role, you’ll shape the surfaces where humans and agents work together: work items, boards, lists, backlogs, plans, agent sessions, and the Teamwork Graph context that makes Jira agents uniquely powerful.

You’ll lead a global team of product managers across Australia, the United States, and India. Reporting to Jira’s Head of Product, you’ll operate as an immediate deputy, directly responsible for strategy, team building, and executing major initiatives. You’ll work closely with engineering and design leadership across Atlassian, spend meaningful time with customers, and hold a high quality bar for everything we ship.

Responsibilities:

* **Product Leadership:** Own the multi-year product strategy for how humans and agents do work together in Jira, including new teamwork patterns that emerge as agents take on a larger share of delivery.
* **Core Jira Experience:** Lead the product vision for work items, boards, lists, backlogs, plans, views, and mobile experiences used by both humans and agents.
* **AI & Agent Context:** Define what a Jira agent knows that a generic agent does not, and how the Teamwork Graph turns that context into visibly better outcomes for customers.
* **Customer Adoption:** Drive agent adoption in Jira, including in-product discovery, onboarding, automation and chat adoption, and the path from a user’s first agent invocation to habitual use.
* **Team Leadership:** Build, develop, and scale a large product organization, hiring, coaching, leveling, and managing product managers and PM managers across three geographies.
* **Product Craft:** Set the bar for experience-led product management inside Jira, with a focus on taste, prototype-first thinking, and protecting quality by cutting scope when needed.
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Partner with leaders across Atlassian, especially in the Teamwork Collection and AI groups, resolving duplicated work and aligning teams around shared outcomes.
* **Customer & Market Voice:** Act as the senior product voice with customers and in the market, translating what you learn from real teams into a durable experience vision.

**Who are we?**

Smarsh empowers its customers to manage risk and unleash intelligence in their digital communications. Our growing community of over 6500 organizations in regulated industries counts on Smarsh every day to help them spot compliance, legal or reputational risks in 80+ communication channels before those risks become regulatory fines or headlines. Relentless innovation has fueled our journey to consistent leadership recognition from analysts like Gartner and Forrester, and our sustained, aggressive growth has landed Smarsh in the annual Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing American companies since 2008.

### **Summary**

The VP, Product Management leads Smarsh's product management organization across multiple lines of business, setting strategic direction and owning end-to-end delivery for the product portfolio. Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, this leader translates corporate strategy into an executable, multi-year product roadmap; builds and develops a multi-layered team of Product Managers and Product Owners; and drives business outcomes — bookings, revenue, and market position — across the domains they own.

This specific role assumes full product leadership for an entire suite of products serving the SMB (small and mid-sized businesses) segment which is a huge growth area for Smarsh. Given the progress we are already making in delivering AI based features, this is a great opportunity for a seasoned product leader to further build on this foundation and deliver a product strategy and roadmap to drive further growth.

  

### **How will you contribute?**

***Strategic Leadership***

* Lead, define, represent, and communicate product strategy to all stakeholders, including executive leadership and the Board
* Own the product roadmap and translate corporate strategy into an executable, multi-year plan across all products and product lines
* Serve as the key evangelist for the product portfolio, participating in press activities, conferences, analyst briefings, and discussions with thought leaders and market analysts

***Enterprise Accountability***

* Own product lifecycle management from concept to launch across all products and lines of business
* Accountable for the operational stability, scalability, and business outcomes of the full product portfolio
* Own and report on strategic KPIs — pipeline, bookings, revenue, and product health — to the CPO and executive leadership

***Program Leadership***

* Lead, manage, and mentor a team of Product Managers, Product Owners, and related personnel across multiple lines of business
* Own product planning and the assignment of tasks and deliverables across the product organization
* Assess product development sprints and enhancement opportunities; monitor sprints and evaluate results

***Planning & Investment Management***

* Develop budgets, forecasts, and metrics for the product portfolio
* Analyze proposed product requirements and development programs; prepare return-on-investment analyses; establish time schedules with Engineering and SaaS Operations
* Define pricing and competitive positioning for each product, using market research, cost data, and volume projections

***Cross-Functional Operating Model***

* Lead Product Marketing Managers to assess product mix and marketing strategy; monitor and manage strategic marketing plans for each product or product line
* Collaborate with stakeholders across Sales, Engineering, Marketing, and Operations to deliver quality products and coordinate go-to-market execution
* Partner with Engineering and SaaS Operations leadership on delivery timelines, capacity, and technical trade-offs

***Partner & Vendor Management***

* Own and manage relationships with key external partners — industry analysts, press, and technology partners — relevant to the product portfolio
* Represent Smarsh in partner, analyst, and customer forums to build market credibility and inform product strategy

Robertshaw is a global design, engineering, and manufacturing company serving the appliance, automotive, and commercial markets. The company develops and manufactures controls and related products for applications including cooking, refrigeration, laundry, water heating, heating, and automotive and commercial systems. Headquartered in Itasca, Illinois, Robertshaw has more than 4,000 employees across 9 countries.

**Position Summary**

Robertshaw is seeking a Senior Director, Product Management to lead the global Product Management organization for its Gas and Water Valve product lines.

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, this role will own product strategy, portfolio direction, market development, and commercial performance for these businesses. The Senior Director will lead a global Product Management team and work closely with Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance to drive profitable growth, strengthen the portfolio, and develop the next generation of products.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will set strategy while remaining directly involved with key customers, product roadmaps, competitive analysis, business cases, pricing, and major product development initiatives.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead global product strategy and portfolio management for Robertshaw's **gas and water valve product lines**.
* Develop product roadmaps based on customer needs, market trends, competitive dynamics, technology, and growth opportunities.
* Identify opportunities to grow the business through new products, applications, customers, and adjacent markets.
* Manage product portfolio performance, including revenue, margin, pricing, product costs, and investment priorities.
* Work directly with key customers and Sales to understand market needs and develop commercial opportunities.
* Partner with Engineering to prioritize product development and ensure resources are focused on the highest-value opportunities.
* Work with Operations and Supply Chain on product cost, manufacturing strategy, capacity, and footprint.
* Lead cross-functional teams through product development, commercialization, and lifecycle management.
* Establish effective Product Management processes and develop a strong global team.
* Evaluate portfolio opportunities to reduce unnecessary customization and complexity while increasing differentiated products and platforms.
* Personally lead critical customer, product, and strategic initiatives when hands-on involvement is required.

**Qualifications**

* Approximately 12 years of progressive experience in Product Management, Engineering, Business Development, Sales, or related technical/commercial roles.
* **Direct experience with gas valves and/or water valves is required**, preferably in appliance, HVAC, water heating, or related industrial applications.
* Demonstrated experience developing product strategy and leading global teams.
* Proven commercial track record with responsibility for product growth, profitability, pricing, or portfolio performance.
* Experience working directly with OEM customers and understanding their product development and purchasing processes.
* Strong understanding of product development, commercialization, and product lifecycle management.
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or related field required; advanced degree preferred.
* Strong cross-functional leadership and influencing skills.
* Willingness to travel globally.

The salary range for this position is $180,000 to $210,000 and eligible to participate in our Management Incentive Program. Actual salary offer may vary based on work experience. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Our current Benefits include: Comprehensive Medical, Dental and Vision Plans, 401k Match, PTO & Paid Holiday Schedule, Legal and Life Insurance, Tuition Assistance. (Benefits listed may vary depending on the nature of your employment and/or work location.)

Description:

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

AIAEC is hiring a Head of Product to lead the strategy, development, commercialization and growth of our SaaS portfolio: current and future products.

We want more than a roadmap manager. We’re looking for a product leader who has taken technology products from idea and discovery through launch, adoption and commercial scale. You’ll lead our Product Owners and UI/UX team, partner closely with Engineering, QA, Support, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing and executive leadership, and make sure AIAEC focuses on the opportunities that matter most to customers and the business.

This role calls for strong product judgment. You’ll guide prioritization, weigh competing opportunities, and direct product and engineering capacity toward the initiatives with the greatest potential for customer adoption, usability and market impact.

**WHAT YOU WILL OWN**

You’ll translate company strategy and market opportunities into clear product strategies, roadmaps and measurable outcomes. Working within AIAEC’s established operating model and product development framework, you’ll drive disciplined execution across the full product lifecycle and help evolve product management practices, standards and tools as we scale.

**Product Strategy & Portfolio Leadership**

* Set the vision, strategy and roadmap for each product based on company goals, market opportunities and customer needs.
* Prioritize across the portfolio when multiple products compete for product and engineering capacity.
* Evaluate new products, features, integrations and markets, and make sure major investments are backed by customer, market and business evidence.
* Assess product and feature readiness before major releases, and partner with the COO and executive team on product direction.

**Discovery & Validation**

* Lead discovery through customer interviews, market and competitive research, workflow analysis and usage data.
* Define problems clearly and assess opportunities before committing significant development resources.
* Gather and synthesize feedback from Customer Success, Sales, Support, pilots and production customers.
* Validate problems and ideas through prototypes, usability tests and experiments, and track product-market fit.

**Product Development**

* Lead execution across the full lifecycle: Idea ? Discovery ? Validation ? Prioritization ? Roadmap ? Backlog ? Development ? Release ? Adoption ? Feedback ? Improvement.
* Turn validated needs into clear requirements, and keep each piece of work traceable to the customer problem it solves.
* Work with Engineering on sequencing, feasibility and delivery. Product owns the what and why; Engineering owns the how.
* Make sure releases meet acceptance, usability and readiness standards, and that post-launch learnings shape future priorities.

**Commercialization & Adoption**

* Partner with Sales, Marketing and Customer Success on personas, ICP, positioning and differentiation.
* Support pricing and packaging discussions, and lead launch and go-to-market readiness planning.
* Help translate product capabilities into clear customer value for Sales and Marketing.
* Track adoption after launch, remove friction, and keep all teams aligned on product capabilities and roadmap direction.

**Product Experience & Accessibility**

* Improve usability, workflows, consistency, engagement and satisfaction across web and mobile products.
* Work with UI/UX, Engineering, Security and Compliance to bring accessibility requirements into product planning.
* Build accessibility into design and development from the start, including WCAG, ADA digital accessibility, accessibility testing and VPAT requirements for public-sector and enterprise customers.

**Product Organization Leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the Product Owners and UI/UX professionals who report to you, with clear goals and accountability.

jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.desc:
**About Volley**
================

Volley Automation is building the future of parking through fully automated robotic parking systems. Our mission is to create sustainable parking solutions that are compact, efficient, and adaptable throughout a building’s lifecycle, while making EV charging easier and more accessible.

Are you intrigued by the idea of putting cars away with robots? Do you hate parking? Do you love parking? If so, we’d love to talk.

Volley Automation builds fully automated parking. Drivers hand off their car at the entry bay and walk away. From there the building takes over: AGVs move vehicles on trays, vertical conveyors move them between floors, and a controls and software stack orchestrates everything. The result is a garage that fits more cars into less concrete, in exactly the urban cores where parking is most expensive to build. Our systems go into real buildings, on real construction schedules, with real occupancy dates. That constraint shapes everything about how we build, develop, and engineer our product.

**The Role**
------------

* Turn customer and market evidence into product decisions: segment definition, configuration and pricing structure, feature go/no-go. Evidence means site visits, operator and owner interviews, and win/loss definitions and not a survey deck someone else built
* Articulate a product vision and get a company that does not yet agree to align behind it, in front of the executive team, the board, customers, and all the way through the entire org - especially the engineering team. You have held the line against per-project one-offs quietly becoming the product

* Experience with a product where the buyer and the user are different people with different definitions of value (developer and owner on one side, driver or parking spot owner/user on the other)
* Has owned a product's direction as well as its delivery. Can point to a roadmap you authored rather than inherited, and explain what you cut and why as well as what was executed on and why
* Owns a cross-functional development roadmap and plan spanning engineering, operations, commercial, and finance with time estimates that are aggressive and still real. Experience delivering this roadmap against an externally fixed date (construction schedule, customer opening, capital project milestone), where the date does not move because a certain department needs or wants it to
* Runs dependency mapping, critical path, and a risk register as habits, with suppliers, contract manufacturers, integrators, and long-lead components tracked as schedule dependencies
* Can close the loop from our Denver HQ and field deployments by turning commissioning, operational friction, and customer feedback into requirements and backlog items

**Required qualifications**
---------------------------

* 8+ years combined, with real depth on both sides of the product owner and program execution fronts. At least 3 years owning a product and at least 3 years owning a program outcome, which may overlap
* Experience with product definition and/or technical program execution with AGVs, AMRs, robotics, material handling, warehouse automation, or vertical transportation
* BS in engineering (ME, EE, or CS) or equivalent hands-on background. Must be able to read an architecture, interrogate a design decision, and push back credibly on a technical effort estimate
* Commercially literate enough to be believed by the CEO and the board: argues a feature in dollars, payback, and segment access
* Startup mode: ambiguity, thin process, influence over authority
* Travel roughly 25-35% for customers, suppliers, and installations

**Desired qualifications**
--------------------------

* Capital equipment product management: long sales cycles, six and seven figure deals, pricing and configuration structure, service and warranty definitions
* Ran a design partner program, customer advisory board, or equivalent structured voice-of-customer mechanism
* Safety-critical or code-reg

**Role Summary**
----------------

Some of Temporal's most important product work begins inside Engineering. It may span the server, Cloud infrastructure, security, capacity, core primitives, SDKs, developer tooling, and AI without arriving as a finished market-facing roadmap. We need a senior product marketing leader who can earn Engineering's trust, understand what is coming, and decide which capabilities require positioning, technical proof, a launch, or a focused adoption plan.

Working directly with the VP of Product Marketing, you will own product-facing Product Marketing across Cloud and platform architecture, Core and SDKs, developer experience, and AI. You will manage a Principal-level Product Marketing Engineer and a Staff Product Marketing Engineer. You will also work closely with Product, Engineering, Developer Relations, Documentation, Sales, Solutions Architecture, and the Solutions and GTM Director.

This is a working leader role. You will personally lead the most important product and portfolio narratives, launch decisions, and adoption programs with the VP. You will set priorities across the portfolio and bring Product Marketing into roadmap discussions early enough to affect the outcome. As the product and market change, you will adjust the team's priorities without losing ownership of the work already underway.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Build direct, durable relationships with engineering leaders and individual engineers across Temporal, including technical areas that do not have dedicated Product Management coverage.
* Maintain a clear view of the Product and Engineering roadmap. Assess each capability against customer need, market opportunity, competitive context, and GTM importance. Decide what requires research, positioning, technical proof, adoption guidance, a launch, or no external announcement.

* Own product and portfolio positioning across Temporal's open-source technology, Cloud offering, core primitives, SDKs, pre-deployment and production features, and AI capabilities.
* Explain the customer value of work on reliability, scalability, performance, availability, security, capacity, migration, and developer tooling without overstating or simplifying the claims.
* Write and edit the positioning and messaging for the company's most important products and launches. Set the quality bar for product narratives across the team.
* Own customer interviews as part of Product Marketing's rotating case-study program and set the quality bar for the team. Capture the customer's problem, decision, implementation, and results. Use that evidence in launches, adoption programs, and recommendations to Product and Engineering.
* Hire, develop, and set priorities for the Product Marketing Engineers. Give them the access and authority to investigate important technical questions and turn their findings into proof, launch and adoption guidance, and specific product feedback.
* Own Temporal's technology ecosystem strategy. Decide which partner categories and integrations matter, set the portfolio narrative, and coordinate joint launches with Product, Engineering, Business Development, the Product Marketing Engineers, and the Solutions and GTM Director.
* Meet customers regularly at least 3 to 4 customers per month.
* Regularly supporting strategic sales deals and collaborating with key sales stakeholders.
* Make clear tradeoffs. Decide which launches need a full company motion, which need focused technical communication, and which do not need a launch at all.

**What You Will Bring**
-----------------------

* Significant product marketing experience with developer tools, cloud infrastructure, open-source software, distributed systems, data infrastructure, or another deeply technical product.

jobs.desc:
**Company Description**

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**

***Who*** **We're Looking For:**

We are looking for a Director of Product Management to lead a team of PMs as well as own the product strategy for empowering developers on the Now platform to build and take their applications to production faster. These areas include developer reach, testing, sandboxing, metering, and deployment of AI and human generated code.

As agentic build tools compress the time it takes to author a change, the bottleneck moves downstream. Testing and deploying safely to production is already one of the loudest customer asks and one of the sharpest pain points on the platform. When changes originate from agents as well as people, and arrive at a much higher rate, the ability to validate and trust them quickly stops being a quality-of-life improvement and becomes a precondition for platform growth. You will lead the team that enables this for developers.

This is not four adjacent feature areas with a shared manager. Customers experience the SDLC as one motion, and the central product challenge of this role is the connective tissue: a sandbox that behaves like the instance you will deploy to, a test suite that knows what changed, a release path that carries the evidence, and a model for building directly in production that an admin can actually govern. You set the strategy that makes their roadmaps resolve into a single lifecycle rather than four products that ship past each other.

The scope is deeply technical and close to execution. The Developer Reach feature area alone unlocks a path to building in production that admins can manage at scale without losing control, and it demands real technical depth to steer. You will also carry a broad surface, over twenty product areas, with the escalation volume that comes with it, and you will need to run that operational load without letting it consume the strategic work.

**What you get to do in this role:**

* Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap across Developer Reach, Developer Sandboxes, Agentic Testing, and Release Ops, and define how they compose into one lifecycle from authored change to governed, audited deployment.
* Build, lead, and develop a team of PMs, one per area. Set a clear standard for product craft, coach PMs on strategy and execution, and hold the bar on the seams between them: shared primitives, consistent models, and a single coherent customer narrative.
* Set product direction for validating AI-originated change at scale: what it means to trust an agent's output, what evidence a release needs to carry, and how much of the test and review burden can be automated without losing accountability.
* Drive the Developer Reach strategy, including the product model for building in production with admin control, guardrails, and reversibility at enterprise scale.
* Define the sandbox strategy: provisioning speed, production parity, data handling, and the developer experience of getting a safe place to work in seconds rather than days.
* Own the release governance path end to end, including the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, and the gating model that makes those tradeoffs explicit rather than accidental.

jobs.title: Vice President of Product
jobs.desc:
**About Onfleet**

Onfleet is the last-mile delivery platform behind millions of deliveries every month for thousands of businesses around the world. We enable shippers to manage deliveries across their private fleet, carriers, and couriers. We make it easy for dispatchers to plan and run their operations, drivers to execute deliveries, and recipients to get real-time tracking and notifications. Our customers span grocery, prepared meals, pharmacy, flowers, furniture, and more.

### **The Role**

We're looking for a **Vice President of Product** to lead Product at Onfleet, owning how our strategy gets translated into roadmaps and how roadmaps turn into shipped, adopted products. Your job is to sharpen our strategy where needed and define how the Onfleet product suite evolves as we scale up in a fast-growing market. This is a hands-on leadership seat where you'll stay close to the details and roll up your sleeves when the team needs it.

You'll report to our CEO and lead Product Management, Design, and User Research. You’ll also work closely with Engineering, QA, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Experience. As our senior-most product leader, you'll sit on our Strategic Leadership Team and represent Product in company planning.

### **What You'll Do**

* Own the product roadmap that delivers on our strategy, and update both as our market and target customers change.
* Prioritize aggressively by committing to a few well-scoped bets per quarter and saying no to other competing initiatives.
* Build deep knowledge of the last-mile delivery industry and our core users: shippers, carriers and couriers, dispatchers, drivers, and recipients.
* Lead quarterly and annual planning with Engineering and go-to-market leaders, and partner with them to set company goals that tie product work to business outcomes.
* Own how we gather, prioritize, and close the loop on product feedback from customers, Sales, CX, and other internal teams.
* Coordinate work across squads so dependencies and risks surface early, and keep one roadmap view the whole company can see.
* Connect product success metrics to company metrics, and build a team habit of defining success before launch and acting on what adoption data shows.
* Represent Product internally and with our board of directors, customer advisory boards, and key customers.
* Foster a collaborative team culture and think ahead about team structure, process, and tooling.
* Coach the team and define clear growth paths for each member.

### **What You'll Bring**

* You have 10+ years in B2B SaaS product roles, including 5+ years leading product teams and 3+ years as Director of Product or above.
* You've run Product at a Series B+ company generating tens of millions of dollars in ARR.
* You've led a product through a move upmarket into enterprise.
* You've directly hired, managed, and developed Product Managers, Designers, and User Researchers.
* You have significant UX and design experience, and you champion it across the company. You've overseen teams that run usability tests, user interviews, and experiments.
* You've partnered with Engineering as equals: scoping work together before committing, keeping scope stable once work starts, and shipping in small iterations.
* You've run market research to size opportunities in a customer base and adjacent markets.
* You make roadmap calls by weighing customer evidence, usage data, strategy, and business impact, and you explain the trade-offs clearly.
* You're analytical, using data to make decisions and hold yourself and your team to the numbers.
* You've built or managed a Product Operations function, with working fluency in tools like Jira, Productboard, and Amplitude.
* You communicate clearly in writing and in person.
* You're highly organized and focused on outcomes.

### **Nice To Have**

* Experience in last-mile logistics or delivery.

### **What We Offer**

* Remote-first work environment with quarterly domestic travel
* Generous employee stock options

jobs.title: Head of PMO & Product Operations
jobs.desc:
Head of PMO & Product Operations

As the Head of PMO & Product Operations at Capital One, you will build and run the operating backbone for a complex, multi-team organization. That means owning how work flows, how capacity gets planned and allocated, where the system can run leaner, and how this organization connects with the other organizations it depends on and serves. You will work with senior leaders across the company to shape an operating model built to scale, then lead a team that turns that model into steady, repeatable execution.

**About the Team:**  
This team operates a portfolio of product and risk operations teams with roughly 200 associates that drive impact across our entire enterprise. The leader in this org will play a key horizontal role across various verticals reporting directly to the Managing Vice President of Product.

**Responsibilities of the Head of PMO & Product Operations:**
-------------------------------------------------------------

* Owning the operating model for the organization: how priorities are set, how capacity is planned, and how work is sequenced and tracked across teams
* Driving efficiency and capacity management across the system: identifying bottlenecks, rebalancing load, and ensuring the organization's resourcing matches its highest priority commitments
* Designing and running the mechanisms (planning cycles, governance forums, reporting cadences) that give leadership visibility into delivery health, risk, and tradeoffs as they emerge
* Serving as the connective layer between this organization and the ones it interconnects with: aligning dependencies, surfacing cross-org risks early, and brokering tradeoffs so commitments made across boundaries actually hold
* Leading and developing a team of program and project managers and operations associates, setting the standards and tools they use to manage complex, dynamic work
* Partnering with senior stakeholders to translate strategy into an executable plan, and refining that plan as priorities and constraints shift
* Building scalable, repeatable processes that cut down on ad hoc firefighting and make the organization more predictable over time

**The person will:**
--------------------

* Think in systems: able to see how capacity, dependencies, and incentives interact across an organization, not just within a single project
* Exhibit outstanding influencing skills to drive alignment across teams and leaders who do not report to them
* Bring a proven track record of standing up or significantly maturing a PMO, operations, or similar operating model function
* Display a passion for coaching and developing a team through a clear, consistent leadership style
* Communicate with precision and credibility at all levels: translate operational complexity into clear choices for executives, and clear direction for teams

**Basic Qualifications:**
-------------------------

* Bachelor’s Degree or Military experience
* At least 10 years of project management experience
* At least 5 years of people management experience

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Masters / MBA degree
* 12+ years of project management experience
* 6+ years of people management experience
* PMP, Lean, Agile or Six Sigma certification
* Exceptional communication and collaboration skills
* Excellent problem solving and influencing skills

At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position.

The minimum and maximum full-time annual salaries for this role are listed below, by location. Please note that this salary information is solely for candidates hired to perform work within one of these locations, and refers to the amount Capital One is willing to pay at the time of this posting. Salaries for part-time roles will be prorated based upon the agreed upon number of hours to be regularly worked.

Richmond, VA: $217,000 - $247,700 for Sr. Director, Project Mgmt  
McLean, VA: $238,700 - $272,400 for Sr. Director, Project Mgmt

jobs.desc:
Order.co is the System of Action for the Office of the CFO, transforming the way businesses purchase and pay into an intuitive, B2C-like shopping experience. Order.co leverages embedded AI agents and embedded financial products to reinvent the way businesses connect with their vendors.

End users enjoy a seamless, zero-training buying experience, while finance and procurement leaders gain a single platform to orchestrate how the business “should operate”. The result is an all-in-one solution that serves as a gravitational pull for spend and data, automating and eliminating procurement and finance workflows from requisition to reconciliation along the way.

Order.co is on the cutting edge of B2B Agentic Commerce, poised to be the market leader in creating a more predictive, prescriptive, and personalized experience for users.

Founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York City, Order.co oversees nearly half a billion in annualized spend across hundreds of customers like WeWork, SoulCycle, Lume, and [solidcore]. Order.co has raised $75M in funding from industry-leading investors like MIT, Stage 2 Capital, Rally Ventures, 645 Ventures, and more. Order.co has been proudly named a 50 to Watch by Spend Matters and a Best Place to Work by BuiltIn and Inc. Magazine.

**The role**
------------

The Director of Product, Buy owns the buying experience and the product decisions that shape marketplace economics. This is the pillar closest to where customers experience value every day: finding the right product, at the right price, from the right supplier, and knowing what happens after the order is placed.

Catalog quality, supplier coverage, sourcing intelligence, and fulfillment reliability shape both the customer experience and the cost of serving it. You will lead product work across those levers, partner closely with Marketplace and vendor operations, and measure the contribution of Buy product changes to purchasing volume, margin, and cost-to-serve.

You will establish clear PM ownership across catalog and search, sourcing and fulfillment, and the vendor network, building and developing a team as staffing and delivery capacity permit. You will be accountable for defined outcomes, not a backlog.

**What you will own**

### **The buying experience**

* Catalog, search, and product discovery, including how customers find what they need and how we guide them toward better choices.
* Sourcing and substitution: presenting alternatives on price, availability, and delivery speed, and making the better choice the easy one.
* Cart construction, order placement, and the pre-purchase journey.
* Fulfillment and order tracking, including how we communicate delays, exceptions, and partial shipments.
* The experience across multi-location customers, where a regional manager, a site lead, and a central procurement team may need different views of the same activity.

### **Marketplace economics and cost-to-serve**

* Catalog coverage and quality across customer needs, including how we prioritize which gaps to close.
* Product levers that influence marketplace margin, including sourcing, substitution, catalog quality, and the cost of fulfilling orders.
* Product and automation changes that reduce supplier onboarding effort and cost per supplier, with Marketplace and vendor operations.
* Product improvements to manual vendor workflows, portal automation, and exception handling. Measure their contribution to lower operating cost with the operational owner; this role does not own the vendor-operations team or its entire budget.

### **Vendor commerce integration**

* Product strategy and requirements for order transmission, supplier portals, catalog feeds, and EDI connections to vendors, in partnership with Engineering and vendor operations.
* The product decisions that make orders reach suppliers reliably and at scale.
* Partnership with Engineering on which integrations to build, automate, improve, or retire.

If your goal is to build a career that makes a difference, consider joining the dedicated people of the Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS). In addition to a great location and rewarding and meaningful work, we offer:

**Description of Job**
----------------------

**CoBEES what is it?**

The Colorado Benefits Eligibility and Enrollment Systems (CoBEES) is a cross-agency portfolio of information technology systems, subsystems, applications, interfaces, training, and communications managed and maintained by the State of Colorado to deliver access to public assistance and medical coverage programs for Coloradans. The CoBEES portfolio includes the Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS), Program Eligibility and Application Kit (PEAK), PEAK Pro, Electronic Document Management System (EDMS), MyColorado Benefits, and the Joint Agency Interoperability (JAI) program. CoBEES supports multiple state departments—operating through a collaborative governance and product operating model between the Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) and the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF)—to administer critical state benefits such as Medicaid, Child Health Plan Plus (CHP+), SNAP, WIC, and TANF. The principal users of these systems include county benefit eligibility technicians, state program administrators, and program participants across Colorado.

  
  
  
  
**What will you be doing?**

Leading a joint CDHS-HCPF-CDEC-OIT product management organization, the HOP oversees day-to-day product ownership of systems including CBMS, PEAK, and Joint Agency Interoperability (JAI). This position works in close partnership with CDHS’s Business, Innovation, Technology, Security Division (BITS), HCPF’s Health Information Office (HIO), the Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT), and contracted vendor partners to ensure CoBEES technologies support end users while advancing product management maturity and best practices across the portfolio. This position provides direct supervisory oversight of the CBMS, PEAK, and JAI product teams and serves as a collaborative executive partner with senior leaders across both departments, including HCPF’s Medicaid Chief Operations Officer and Deputy Director of the Health Information Office, as well as CDHS’s Office Director for Economic Security and Office Director of Infrastructure, to ensure coordinated governance and strategic direction of CoBEES. The HOP maintains joint accountability to the Executive Directors of both CDHS and HCPF. **Description of Job**
----------------------

**CoBEES what is it?**

The Colorado Benefits Eligibility and Enrollment Systems (CoBEES) is a cross-agency portfolio of information technology systems, subsystems, applications, interfaces, training, and communications managed and maintained by the State of Colorado to deliver access to public assistance and medical coverage programs for Coloradans. The CoBEES portfolio includes the Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS), Program Eligibility and Application Kit (PEAK), PEAK Pro, Electronic Document Management System (EDMS), MyColorado Benefits, and the Joint Agency Interoperability (JAI) program. Leading a joint CDHS-HCPF-CDEC-OIT product management organization, the HOP oversees day-to-day product ownership of systems including CBMS, PEAK, and Joint Agency Interoperability (JAI). jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.desc:
Courier Health is on a mission to solve one of the biggest and most meaningful opportunities in healthcare: reinvent how people living with chronic and rare diseases are supported.

We are building the future of patient engagement for life sciences companies. Our software is leveraged by biopharma companies to support patients in their complex journey from diagnosis to initiating and remaining on therapy to achieve optimal health outcomes.

### **Come Build with Us**

We're a NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We're an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. If that sounds like your kind of place, we think you'll love it here.

### **The Opportunity**

Courier Health is at an inflection point. We exist to get patients faster, better access to life-saving therapies, and product helps to shape decisions related to which patients we reach next and how soon.

As Director of Product, you will lead a team of product managers covering the full platform, reporting directly to the CEO. You will also keep a hand in the work running discovery, writing the spec, making the call — on the bets that matter most.

The roadmap here is not handed down. You will decide what we build, in what order, and what we deliberately don't do, in a market where the right answer is rarely obvious and the stakes are patients starting therapy. If you have led product teams inside someone else's operating model and want to define your own, this is the seat.

### **What You'll Build**

**A product team that makes its own calls.** You will coach to a standard in weekly one on ones and roadmap reviews, raise the bar on writing and discovery, and give your PMs enough room to be wrong and get better. The goal is a team that can size a bet and defend it without you in the room.

**A roadmap the whole company can bet on.** Sales, implementation, and engineering all plan against what product says is coming. You will set the sequencing across a growing customer base, make the tradeoffs between what one strategic client needs and what the platform needs, and say no clearly enough that people trust the yes. Commitments hold, and when they change, everyone knows why in time to act.

**Discovery grounded in how patients actually get to therapy.** Our users are the people running patient support programs, field teams, and hub operations. You will get your team in front of them, translate what you hear into product, and build the customer and market fluency that makes our roadmap hard to copy. Strong opinions are welcome here. Strong opinions without customer contact are not.

### **What Makes You Successful**

* 10+ years in product management at a B2B software company, with a track record of shipping products enterprise customers renewed and expanded.
* 5+ years managing product managers. You have hired, coached, and given hard feedback that made someone better.
* Proven ownership of a roadmap end to end from customer discovery and strategy through launch and measured outcomes, not just execution against someone else's plan.
* Strong technical fluency. You can work through data models, API integrations, and architectural tradeoffs with engineers and hold your own. Coding is not required. Depth is.
* Excellent judgment under ambiguity. You can make a call with incomplete information, explain the reasoning, and change course without drama when the evidence shifts.
* Exceptional written communication. You think in documents, and your specs make the decision obvious.
* Comfortable working directly with senior customer stakeholders, including the conversations nobody wants to have.
* Experience building process where none existed, and the restraint to keep it minimal.

You will lead revenue, pricing, packaging, margin, and cost-reduction efforts across Product and Engineering, and pair that near-term revenue strategy with the long-term product and company strategy that sets Motive's direction. You will report to the Sr. Director of Product, build your own team, and work daily with senior leaders across the company.

You are an exceptional partner and a rigorous analyst: someone who earns trust across Product, Engineering, Finance, and Go-to-Market, and who turns complex data into clear decisions. You are comfortable moving between a financial model and a multi-year strategy, and you take ownership of results, not just recommendations.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Drive revenue expansion strategy for Motive's core and growing suite of software SKUs, and own pricing and packaging governance from analysis through launch and measurement.
* Define how Motive views and manages the cost of R&D spend across devices, cellular, IoT, and software services, and own the cost data foundation behind product-level margin and COGS.
* Partner with product line leaders to identify and deliver revenue generation & cost-reduction initiatives that improve gross margin.
* Size new product lines and adjacencies, and work with product leadership to run proofs of concept and decide whether to bring new products to market.
* Shape long-term product and company strategy, turning market, customer, and competitive insight into multi-year plans and investment choices.
* Run the operating cadence for R&D strategy, including planning, business reviews, and executive reporting.
* Hire, build, and lead a team of strategy and operations professionals.

### **What We're Looking For:**

* 2+ years of experience in management consulting or investment banking.
* 5+ years of operating experience in a business operations or corporate strategy role.
* Advanced financial modeling skills, with the ability to turn analysis into clear recommendations for executives.
* Track record of driving measurable business outcomes, such as revenue, margin, or cost, rather than recommendations alone.
* Proven success partnering and influencing across functions and levels without direct authority.
* Experience hiring, developing, and leading a team.

USA Lacrosse, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation, is a Recognized Sports Organization of the United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee who proudly serves the sport by bringing the energy and excitement of our efforts to players, coaches, and officials every time they step on the field. TechBootcamp.com is an online career education company. We are starting with the Data Center Accelerator, which helps U.S. tradespeople, veterans and suitable career changers transition into data center roles.

**THE ROLE**

We are hiring a senior Head of Product / Lead Instructor to build the program from the ground up and own its development, delivery and improvement.

This is a leadership role. You will be responsible for the complete learning product and the team that supports our students, and you will work directly with the founder on strategy, priorities and resources.

jobs.desc:
In the early 1980s at Bell Labs, Gerald Ash and his colleagues questioned a rule that AT&T's long-distance network had followed for decades; a call climbed a fixed hierarchy of switches until it found an open path. They modeled the idea, simulated it, and tested it until it held. In 1984, AT&T put Dynamic Nonhierarchical Routing (DNHR) into the national network, which became the basis of global real-time telephony routing that came after it.

At Mercury, customers reach us through Dashboard, Mobile, Command, our API, and Model Context Protocol (MCP). Each request should take the best path to the work, whatever surface it starts on. We're looking for a Head of Product, Interfaces to design that network. You'll set one direction across these surfaces and lead the PMs who build them. You'll also build the shared capabilities that let every Mercury team reach customers well: navigation, tasks, notifications, and agent interactions. AI is central to the role. The job is to find where AI removes real work, and to make it dependable enough to trust with money.

This is a hands-on leadership role reporting to the VP of Product. You’ll develop people while staying close to customers, prototypes, product decisions, and shipped quality.

* *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.*

* Set the product direction for Interfaces. Connect Dashboard, Mobile, Command, and API/MCP through a clear view of customer needs and the role of each surface
* Lead and develop the PM team. Build clear ownership, coach product judgment, hire strong people, and help the team deliver excellent work
* Shape Mercury’s AI experience. Partner with the Command team to turn new AI capabilities into useful products that help customers complete financial work
* Improve the core product experience. Make it easier for customers to understand their finances, find the right action, and move between devices and workflows
* Build shared capabilities. Help Mercury teams deliver through common foundations such as navigation, tasks, notifications, and agent interactions
* Make quality part of product development. Work with engineering, design, data, and research partners to evaluate behavior, understand failures, and improve through evidence
* Design for customer control. Make consequential actions understandable, permissions clear, and progress and results easy to inspect
* Connect the portfolio across Mercury. Partner with teams building banking\*, Spend, Books, Payroll, and other products to bring their capabilities into shared experiences
* Own the tradeoffs. Balance immediate customer needs, new opportunities, and the platform investments that make future work faster and better

### **What we’re looking for:**

* 10+ years of direct product management experience, with 5+ years leading product managers: hiring, coaching, org design, and performance management
* A track record of shipping products that customers value, with a clear account of your own decisions and contribution
* Experience leading PMs and working across multiple teams or a broad product area; enthusiasm for developing people while staying close to the work

jobs.desc:
**About Us**
============

At Bucket Listers, we're all about unleashing life’s full potential and having a blast along the way! Our goal is to encourage people to make lasting memories, forge new connections, and embark on new adventures through our platform of curated experiences. Our vibrant community of explorers relies on us to help them find the coolest events and experiences any day of the week.

We're on a mission to make magic happen, and we're searching for enthusiastic individuals to join our incredible team. We're not just dreamers; we're seasoned explorers ourselves, and we can't wait to share our infectious positivity and limitless inspiration with the world.

### **The Opportunity**

As Director of Product for SafeSend, you will own that surface and lead its evolution into an AI-driven, agentic gather-prepare-deliver experience on Thomson Reuters’ CoCounsel platform and open it up so firms and partners can build on it.

**The opportunity:**

* Firms are consolidating fragmented point tools into one connected workflow and want a single partner to deliver it.
* Taxpayers expect a modern, mobile, trustworthy way to share documents and receive their return.
* Document data extraction is going AI-native; firms want agentic preparation and review and are adopting it now.
* Firms increasingly want to build on open APIs so their own portals, data and reporting stay connected as the market converges.
SafeSend sits at the center of all four. This is a build-and-converge mandate — shaping a market-defining product, not maintaining a mature one.  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Deliver SafeSend. Own the SafeSend portfolio end to end — Gather, Organizers, e-Sign, Delivery, Returns and Extensions — season over season, at the reliability and scale that tax-filing peaks demand.
* Converge SafeSend and TaxCaddy. Bring the best of SafeSend and TaxCaddy together into one Gather & Deliver experience for every firm and taxpayer[CH1]
* Componentize the portfolio. Turn each part of SafeSend into reusable workflow components that can be recomposed across the gather – prepare – deliver flow and used across the broader CoCounsel platform, rather than locked inside a single app.
* Enable expanded SafeSend access via APIs and orchestration. Expand the SafeSend API surface — open APIs, events and integrations — as a first-class capability, so firms and partners embed SafeSend in their own portals and workflows and keep their tools, data and reporting connected, with orchestration so AI agents and partner systems can coordinate gather and delivery programmatically.
Deliver agentic Gather & Deliver through CoCounsel. Bring agentic Gather — and AI-driven extraction, preparation and review — into the SafeSend experience on the CoCounsel platform, so more of the work shifts from staff to the platform while the firm stays in control.  

**What success looks like:**

* Firms experience one connected Gather & Deliver workflow, whatever ecosystem they run today.
* The SafeSend API is something firms and partners actively build on, not a bespoke integration project.
* Firms reach AI-driven, agentic preparation and review through SafeSend, season over season.
Taxpayers get a simpler, faster, more trustworthy experience — and firms see measurably less manual work.  

**Required Qualifications:**

Strong stakeholder management and a proven record of building high-performing teams

* Background in tax & accounting, fintech, or document / data-pro
