**This is a hybrid position, with an expectation of being onsite up to four days per week.**

**Lead the Way to Intelligent Banking with Us!**

You might not think about what happens behind the scenes when you check your bank balance or deposit a check from your phone, but we do. Every day.

Kinective empowers banks and credit unions to move beyond keeping up with technology to shaping the future of banking. Our platform seamlessly connects the right tools, delivers real-time data, and drives smarter operations for more than 4,000 financial institutions nationwide.

We are a fast-growing team built on individual ownership, company-wide collaboration, and setting industry-leading standards. Here, new ideas are encouraged, candid feedback is welcomed, and your growth truly matters as much as the company's. At Kinective, we are leading the way to intelligent banking together and enjoying the journey along the way.

**Why This Role Matters**

Every role at Kinective exists to move the needle for our clients, partners, and the financial institutions we serve.

As the Director of Product Management, Data Intelligence, you will guide the Data Intelligence (DI) roadmap and make sure it lands in the market. You will work hand in hand with Product Marketing, Marketing, and Sales to bring new capabilities to market successfully, and you will lead the DI product team to deliver the roadmap with consistency and quality. You will also be a key partner on cross-product initiatives that connect DI to the rest of the Kinective platform, so banks and credit unions can turn their data into action and measurable business results.

You will report to the VP of Product, Data Intelligence, and carry the strategy into day-to-day execution through your team and your cross-functional partners.

**What You'll Own**

**Roadmap Leadership**

* Guide the Data Intelligence roadmap in partnership with the VP of Product, turning product line strategy into clear priorities, sequencing, and release plans.
* Bring together customer feedback, market trends, competitive insight, and financial institution use cases to make well-reasoned prioritization calls.
* Prioritize scalable, repeatable capabilities over custom one-off requests, and communicate the "why" behind roadmap decisions to internal teams and clients.
* Keep the roadmap connected to commercial outcomes, including packaging, pricing, and the use cases that matter most to banks and credit unions.

**Go-to-Market Partnership**

* Partner directly with Product Marketing, Marketing, and Sales so every launch has clear positioning, messaging, enablement, and a plan that sales teams can use right away.
* Make sure launches are grounded in what the product can demonstrate today, with a clear view of what is coming next.
* Bring the voice of the customer and the field back into the roadmap through client conversations, advisory programs, and regular feedback loops with Sales and Services.
* Support sales and client conversations as a product expert where DI value, use cases, and roadmap direction need to be told well.

**Execution Leadership**

* Lead and develop the DI product team, including Product Managers and Product Owners, setting clear expectations, coaching on craft, and building strong operating habits.
* Drive execution on the roadmap with Engineering, UX, Services, and Support through clear requirements, healthy Agile practices, and predictable delivery.
* Run the operating cadence for DI, including planning, release readiness, KPI tracking, risk and dependency management, and status reporting to the VP and leadership.
* Spot risks early, remove blockers, and escalate with options and recommendations.

**Cross-Product and Cross-Functional Initiatives**

* Lead or co-lead cross-product initiatives where DI capabilities power broader Kinective solutions, platform work, and solution bundles.
* Partner with Platform, AI, and other product lines to align requirements, sequencing, and delivery across team

Founded in 2008, DoubleVerify (DV) is the leading independent provider of marketing measurement software, data and analytics that authenticates the quality and effectiveness of digital media for the world's largest brands and media platforms. Fred Luddy started ServiceNow with a simple idea: automate the tedious work so people can focus on what matters. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. jobs.title: Director of Product Strategy, Commerce
jobs.desc:
**Overview**

Microsoft Commerce is placing large bets across Consumer, Merchant, Partner, and Payments in a market being reshaped by agentic commerce and a live contest over the protocols and payer models that will govern it.

We are looking for a **Director of Product Strategy, Commerce** to own the analytical and narrative spine of Commerce strategy: the person who can look across the whole agentic-commerce field and our position in it, size the opportunity, name the bet, and prove the business model works — then write it so it lands in the room.

This is an individual-contributor force-multiplier to the VP. The role sets net-new strategic direction that the pillar teams build against, holds the entire Commerce picture at once, and reaches a defensible call: what we bet on, who pays and why, how big the prize is, and the story that carries it through review. The ideal candidate reasons from first principles about business models and market opportunity, brings structure to high-stakes product decisions, and turns dense analysis into one clear, defensible narrative. Leverage comes from the quality of the thinking and the clarity of the call rather than the size of a team.

In this role you will own strategy across the full Commerce portfolio, including:

* Market & competitive strategy: a first-principles POV on agentic commerce — the protocol landscape, the incentives of each major player, and where our advantage is real.
* Monetization & business-model design: who pays and why across Consumer, Merchant, and Partner; payer models, methods, and sequencing that give the strategy a working economic engine.
* Opportunity sizing & forecasting: market, feature, and monetization sizing from first principles — TAM SAM capturable, unit economics, ARR and ROI.
* Decision frameworks for major bets: structure for high-stakes, ambiguous calls — build / buy / partner, sequencing, reversible vs. one-way-door, and where to place a bet across pillars.
* Cross-thread synthesis: one coherent strategy across Consumer, Merchant, Partner, and Payments, with the conflicts surfaced before they collide in review.
* Narrative & decision support: the strategy spine — MMM narrative, FY strategy papers, the investment case — written to land with senior stakeholders.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

AI Experiences employees who live within a 50- mile commute of a designated Microsoft Hub in the U.S. are expected to work from the office at least four days per week. This expectation is subject to local law and may vary by jurisdiction.

 **Responsibilities**

* Own a current, first-principles POV on the agentic-commerce market, the protocol landscape (for example ACP, UCP, AP2, MCP), and where Microsoft’s advantage is real.
* Design and pressure-test monetization: the payer model across Consumer, Merchant, and Partner, the methods, and the sequencing.
* Build the opportunity models and forecasts that let the org rank bets and defend investment asks with numbers, including ARR- and ROI-based justification.
* Bring repeatable decision frameworks to major product bets so the reasoning is structured and legible.
* Synthesize the Consumer, Merchant, Partner, and Payments threads into one coherent strategy and surface where they conflict.
* Turn the analysis into the strategy spine — the MMM narrative, FY strategy papers, and investment cases — and prep the VP with a sharp POV and the two or three things that would change it.
* Operate as a peer to senior leaders: form a POV, defend it, and change it on evidence.

 **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications:**

* Master's Degree in Business Administration or related

jobs.title: Head of Product Led Growth
jobs.desc:
**About Re:Build**
------------------

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate a sophisticated, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as meaningful as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and give to the communities where we operate. The Re:Build Way principles

Re:Build is building Livewire, a launchpad business bringing AI-native software to intuitive wire harness design and manufacturing. The product is real, customers are already using it, and there's still a lot to learn about how the growth engine should work; that's where this role comes in.

We're looking for a hands-on product growth leader who can connect the whole customer journey: how the right users find Livewire, what gets them into the product, what gets them to real value, what brings them back, and what eventually gets them to pay. You'll work closely with Product and also partner with Marketing, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success. Together, you will make that journey measurable and keep a consistent flow of experiments. These experiments will help turn what you learn into better product and growth decisions.

This is a builder role. You should be just as comfortable looking at product behavior as acquisition data, enjoy running experiments, want to talk to users, and be energized by the fact that there isn't a mature growth playbook waiting for you — because you'll help build it. You'll likely start with few or no direct reports. Instead, you will guide external firms, contractors, and internal specialists. See that as an opportunity rather than a limitation.

**What You Get To Do**
----------------------

* Own the growth journey from acquisition through activation, lifecycle and conversion.
* Build a clear view of the customer journey; who's converting, where they get stuck, and whether they're reaching real value.
* Run a steady cadence of experiments across acquisition, onboarding, product experience, lifecycle and conversion.
* Partner with Product to turn user insights into a faster path to value.
* Build the measurement and operating rhythm that helps the team learn and decide faster.
* Drive conversion, retention and expansion with Sales, RevOps and Customer Success.
* Shape positioning and messaging based on customer insight, in partnership with Marketing.
* Direct agencies and specialists to move faster, without outsourcing the thinking.

**What You Bring To The Team**
------------------------------

* Experience in product growth, PLG, lifecycle marketing or a similar role; and you know growth doesn't stop at signup.
* Hands-on experience designing and running experiments, including with imperfect data and small samples.
* Strong partnership with Product, using customer and product data to drive decisions.
* Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited infrastructure.
* Strong quantitative skills funnels, cohorts, conversion and experiment analysis.
* Familiarity with product analytics, CRM/marketing automation, web analytics and experimentation tools.
* Preferred: product-led, self-service or digital commerce experience. Wire harness/CAD/manufacturing expertise not required.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Product-led, self-service, digital commerce or online buying experience.
* Domain expertise in wire harnesses, CAD

Bookings owns the booking flow and everything a pet parent does after booking.

Each team owns a customer journey end to end and pairs with an engineering lead and a designer.

About Seated

Seated exists to help restaurants thrive in an industry defined by thin margins and underutilized capacity. We connect thousands of restaurants with millions of high-intent diners through demand-driven pricing and rewards, helping restaurants fill empty tables, reach new guests, increase visit frequency, and drive profitable incremental revenue.

Since launching, billions of dollars in restaurant spend have flowed through Seated, and hundreds of millions of dollars in rewards have been paid to Seated consumers. Today, Seated operates across 20+ U.S. markets and continues to expand nationally.

Our core marketplace is thriving. Now, we’re focused on expanding the value Seated creates for restaurants and consumers and building the company’s next major growth engine.  
  
See it for yourself: seatedapp.io (restaurant side) · getseated.seatedapp.io (diner side) · Seated on iOS · Seated on Android

Role Overview

Seated is hiring a Director of Product to serve as our first dedicated Product leader, owning product strategy and execution across our consumer and restaurant businesses.

Reporting directly to the CEO, this person will play a key role in shaping Seated’s product direction, identifying and validating new growth opportunities, and translating business priorities into products that create meaningful value for restaurants and consumers.

This is a highly hands-on role. You’ll work directly with our SVP of Engineering and a lean engineering team to drive the full product lifecycle, from customer discovery and data analysis to requirements, prioritization, testing, and launch.

We’re looking for someone who thrives in an environment without established product processes or a large team. You’ll bring structure to how we make product decisions, build a focused roadmap, and help establish the foundation for a scalable Product function as Seated grows.

Responsibilities

* Own product strategy, roadmap, and execution across Seated’s consumer and restaurant products in partnership with the CEO and Engineering
* Identify, evaluate, and validate new product opportunities that can drive Seated’s next stage of growth
* Lead product discovery, customer research, experimentation, and business-case development to inform product decisions
* Explore opportunities across consumer marketplace expansion, restaurant software, AI, and adjacent products

* Establish lightweight product processes, including roadmap planning, requirements documentation, prioritization frameworks, and success metrics

* Develop a deep understanding of consumer behavior, restaurant operator needs, unit economics, and marketplace dynamics
* Help shape the future Product function as Seated grows, including identifying opportunities to expand product and design capabilities

* 7+ years of product management experience, with demonstrated ownership of products from discovery through launch and iteration
* Experience building and shipping products in a startup or high-growth technology company
* Strong consumer product instincts, ideally developed within a marketplace or consumer technology business

jobs.title: Director of Product Marketing, International
jobs.desc:
### **About the Role**

Foxit is looking for a **Director of Product Marketing, International** to define and lead the category strategy, portfolio positioning, and go-to-market approach for our product portfolio across **North America, EMEA, and APAC**.

This is a high-impact leadership role for a product marketer who can operate at both a strategic and executional level. You will shape how Foxit understands the market, where we play, how we win, and how we translate customer and competitive insight into product strategy, messaging, packaging, pricing, and commercial activation.

Reporting to the SVP, Head of Marketing, you will lead market intelligence, original research, segmentation, and positioning across the portfolio. You will work in close partnership with Product leadership to ensure market insight directly informs innovation priorities, roadmap direction, and long-term portfolio strategy. You will also partner closely with Growth Marketing, Integrated Campaigns, Sales, and Customer Success to bring positioning to life in market and support successful product launches globally.

This role is ideal for a senior product marketing leader who thrives in fast-moving B2B software environments, brings strong commercial instincts, and knows how to turn customer insight into differentiated market strategy and measurable business impact.

### **What You’ll Do**

#### **Lead Product Marketing Strategy**

* Define the market, category, and positioning strategy for Foxit’s product portfolio across global regions.
* Develop clear, differentiated messaging and value propositions aligned to target buyers, use cases, and customer needs.
* Own segmentation, buyer personas, pricing and packaging inputs, and portfolio narrative development.
* Ensure product marketing strategy supports both regional go-to-market needs and broader company growth objectives.

#### **Build and Lead the PMM Function**

* Build, lead, and develop a team of Product Marketers, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and capability building.
* Establish PMM operating rhythms and sprint cycles aligned to product, release, and campaign timelines.
* Embed product marketing into R&D and product planning processes, including roadmap reviews, discovery sessions, and sprint reviews.
* Drive strong cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success.

#### **Drive Market Vision and Intelligence**

* Develop and maintain a 1–3 year market vision for each product area, including customer needs, technology shifts, competitive dynamics, and category evolution.
* Own the MRD process across both short-term and long-term planning horizons, translating research and analysis into actionable product and business recommendations.
* Lead original research initiatives to uncover customer insight, validate market direction, and strengthen competitive differentiation.
* Present market narratives, trends, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership, internal stakeholders, and external audiences.

#### **Own Positioning and Portfolio Narrative**

* Lead category definition, competitive differentiation, and positioning strategy across the portfolio.
* Develop and maintain core messaging frameworks and positioning for products, launches, and strategic pivots.
* Partner with Brand, Content, and Integrated Marketing to ensure consistency between product narratives and campaign execution.

jobs.title: Head of Product Marketing
jobs.desc:
**The role**
------------

We're in the midst of the most important buildout in U.S. history, with large growth across energy, transmission, commercial/industrial, housing, and conservation + carbon. Land is the bottleneck for all of these efforts. Aarden is a purpose-built solution to understand, invest in, and get deals done for land-dependent assets.

While only 16 months old, we are already working with the most important landowners and developers in the country, and it's time for the world to know about us. That's where you come in.

As Head of Product Marketing, your job is to show the market how Aarden thinks about land, in public, every week, and use that as a launching point to make Aarden the most influential and important voice in land markets. When a hyperscaler announces a campus, a county passes a moratorium, or a timber owner sells a million acres, you'll use Aarden to figure out what it means within the broader market context, what owners and developers should be doing in response, and what new opportunities it creates. Aarden is used to help clients make decisions like this every day, and your job is to elevate these capabilities to a much broader audience.

Over time, we want Aarden (and its leadership) to be who people turn to when they want to understand how America's land is changing, and we want that attention to turn into conversations with the landowners, developers, and investors who make the world move.

**About Aarden**
----------------

Aarden is the origination and investment partner for people building on and making decisions about American land, starting with the landowners and developers behind the energy & data center buildouts. For institutional timber and farmland owners, that means helping them see what their land could become and how to value it. For developers, it means finding willing owners with viable sites before sinking months of time and capital into a site that faces significant headwinds. For everyone, it means understanding the environmental and social impacts of these important decisions.

Under the hood, our platform combines parcel data, ownership resolution, zoning, community sentiment, and price signals with suitability models and defensible investment analysis.

We're a Seattle-based team, growing quickly and founded in 2025, with expansion plans into NYC in 2027. Four of the ten largest U.S. landowners are already clients, and our committed clients cover roughly 14 million acres of high value land. We have a wonderful cohort of investors as well. Our $4m pre-seed was announced last year but our subsequent fundraising efforts remain undisclosed; you would help us announce this.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* **Hunt for stories.** Read the news every day across data centers, energy, timber, farmland, and land policy, and comment on key events that change land markets (there are a lot of these!).
* **Use Aarden to find the answer.** Work with Aarden technology to figure out what each event means, lay out the options it creates for owners and developers, and back it up with historical and present-day patterns. Our data team will support you in this work.
* **Build Aarden's following on LinkedIn and X.** Publish several times a week across the company's and leadership's channels, and grow those audiences. You'll develop your own voice along the way, too.
* **Tell client stories.** Highlight our clients' efforts and help them grow their businesses with case studies that show how the smartest investors in the country partner with Aarden to drive results for their funds.
* **Turn attention into pipeline.** The stories we tell should help more organizations see the clear benefits of partnering with Aarden.
* **Speak to both sides of the market.** Write for timber and farmland owners who are weighing alternative uses, and for data center developers who are quite literally racing to secure sites. Help each learn about the benefits of working with the other.
* **Make Aarden

jobs.desc:
**About EnerVenue**

———————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————

EnerVenue is a Silicon Valley-based energy infrastructure company commercializing metal-hydrogen battery technology originally developed by NASA for the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station. Founded in 2020 by Stanford Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue adapts this proven aerospace chemistry for grid-scale terrestrial energy storage, delivering batteries with 30,000+ cycle lifetimes, inherent fire-safety, and a 30-year design life.

In 2026, EnerVenue closed a $300 million Series B extension and is well capitalized for growth. Funds are being deployed to build a high-volume manufacturing facility in Changzhou, China, targeting 250 MWh capacity by Q3 2026 and 1 GWh by 2027. EnerVenue has been named one of Time magazine's Top 10 US Green Technology Companies of 2025.

**The Role**

———————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————

The Product Management Director reports directly to the Chief Product Officer and owns the full product lifecycle of EnerVenue's metal-hydrogen energy storage portfolio, from the Ni-H2 vessel and module, to racks, containerized and skid-mounted energy storage systems, and the accompanying BMS/EMS software layer. You are the single point of ownership connecting the market to the technology: translating utility, C&I and international customer needs into a prioritized roadmap, clear product requirements, defensible pricing, and products that R&D can design and the factory can build at scale.

This is a build-and-scale mission rather than a caretaking role. You will establish the product management function from the ground up: the roadmap process, the stage-gate NPI governance, the product cost and margin model, the competitive intelligence engine and the launch playbook. You will align product strategy with the company's gigawatt capacity roadmap, drive continuous reduction of levelized cost of storage (LCOS), and make the disciplined trade-off decisions across performance, cost, certification and time-to-market that determine whether each product wins in its target segment.

**Key Responsibilities**

———————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————

**1. Product Strategy & Roadmap Ownership**

* Define and own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the full metal-hydrogen storage portfolio: cells and vessels, modules, racks, containerized/skid systems, and BMS/EMS software.
* Segment the market by application (utility-scale, C&I, microgrid, long-duration storage, harsh-environment and off-grid) and geography, and define the target product configuration, differentiation and value proposition for each segment.
* Build and maintain the business case for every product line: addressable market, volume forecast, price and cost trajectory, margin, investment requirement and payback.
* Align the product roadmap with the company's gigawatt capacity plan, R&D technology roadmap and go-to-market priorities; arbitrate scope, sequencing and resource allocation across competing initiatives.

**2. Market, Customer & Competitive Intelligence**

* Run a structured voice-of-customer program with utilities, IPPs, developers, EPCs, integrators and channel partners; convert field insight into prioritized requirements.
* Maintain continuous competitive intelligence across LFP and other lithium chemistries, flow batteries, sodium-ion and long-duration storage technologies; quantify EnerVenue's advantage in cycle life, safety, temperature tolerance and total lifetime cost.
* Track policy, incentive, tariff, grid-code and standards developments in target markets, and translate the implications into roadmap and positioning decisions.
* Own LCOS and total-cost-of-ownership models used in customer-facing value engineering and internal product decisions.

**3. Requirements Definition & NPI Governance**

* Author and own market requirement documents (MRD) and product requirement documents (PRD),

**About Pocket**
----------------

At Pocket, we're building the future of human memory.

We believe some of the most valuable information in our lives is lost every day — in conversations, meetings, ideas, and moments that never make it into the digital world.

Pocket changes that.

We've built an AI-powered wearable device that captures real-world conversations and transforms them into searchable, actionable intelligence.

But capturing conversations is just the beginning.

Imagine a world where everything you learn, discuss, and experience can become useful context for the AI tools you already use — and entirely new products that don't exist yet.

That's what we're building.

With hundreds of thousands of devices already in the hands of customers, we're looking for an exceptional **Head of Product** to help define what comes next.

**About the Role**
------------------

We're looking for someone who is **obsessed with AI, exceptional product experiences, and building things that millions of people will love.**

You'll own the entire Pocket product experience — from the moment someone discovers and activates their device to how they interact with their personal knowledge, AI-powered features, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This isn't a role for someone who simply manages a roadmap.

We want a **builder, thinker, and operator** who can turn ambitious ideas into exceptional products.

You'll work directly with the founders and lead product development across hardware, mobile, desktop, AI, and integrations.

**Your mission: Make Pocket one of the most loved and indispensable AI products in the world.**

**What You'll Own**

* Push the boundaries of what is possible with the latest AI models and technologies.
* Build AI-powered experiences that transform conversations into useful knowledge, actions, and personalized intelligence.
* Explore agents, proactive assistants, personal memory, contextual intelligence, and entirely new product categories.
* Experiment rapidly with emerging AI capabilities and bring the best ideas into production.

* Make Pocket deeply connected to the broader AI ecosystem.

* Explore APIs, MCP, agents, and new ways to make captured knowledge actionable.
* Turn Pocket into a powerful source of real-world context for AI applications.

* Own and oversee every major product initiative across the company.

* Drive projects from concept to launch, with clear ownership, priorities, and accountability.
* Establish a culture of rapid experimentation, high standards, and continuous improvement.
* Stay extremely close to customers, their feedback, and how they actually use Pocket.

KeepTruckin builds technology using the latest advancements in AI and computer vision to improve the safety and efficiency of businesses with vehicles. Over one million drivers and 100,000 companies across every industry trust KeepTruckin’s integrated platform to power their operations, prevent accidents and reduce costs.  

At KeepTruckin, we see our hard work rewarded in tangible ways every day, and we believe that intelligence is most powerful when paired with humility. As part of a Global Product Management team, you will be accountable for the long-term profitable growth and marketing of the SFC offering to target market segments, by developing and managing the portfolio through its life cycle phases, according to market needs, the business strategy and targets. jobs.desc:
About the Company

GoGoGrandparent’s (GoGo’s) mission is to help older adults live independently in their home for as long as possible. We do that by tailoring existing on demand apps to the needs of people living with mobility, visual, cognitive and dexterity impairments and letting older adults use them by making a phone call. After ordering, our service becomes a virtual caregiver that monitors the instrumental activities of daily living (mobility, meals, groceries, medication delivery & home management) for tens of thousands of older adults around the United States. We’re profitable, have been around since 2016 & haven’t raised any venture capital financing to date. The company was inspired by the cofounder’s grandmother, who still uses us to this day (she’s turning 95 in March)!

This is a fully remote position located in the United States

Job Summary

The Growth Product Manager will have broad autonomy to identify and act on opportunities in expanding our core service, rides. This is our largest and most mature service line, and improving its conversion funnel can have a meaningful impact on the company. The role includes customer research, working closely with phone operators, data analysis, and running rigorous A/B tests.

  • Own the ‘Rides’ product funnel end to end, from first touch through registration. 
  • Identify and prioritize the highest impact opportunities to improve conversion, using data, operator feedback, and customer insights.
  • Design, run, and analyze A/B tests on phone and CRM flows to drive measurable improvements.

jobs.desc:
We're ~160 people, fully remote, building an AI marketing platform. Our main product is OTTO, which runs a site's SEO on its own - it reads live search data and pushes the technical and on-page fixes itself, nobody queues them up. Around that we've got ad automation for Google and Meta, GBP management for multi-location brands, content gen, and LLM visibility tracking (whether ChatGPT and co are citing you). Autotrader, Hyundai, P&G, Vendasta are some of our customers.
Work happens in pods, 1 PM and 2-4 engineers. You own your pod's roadmap and ship it with them, no veteran PM signing off on your specs first. That's the part most PM roles won't hand you.
Looking for 3+ years PM in B2B SaaS with an actual technical background - eng or QA before PM, or a PM who's been getting into the codebase themselves. You should be able to read Python and TS, write your own SQL, find your way around an API, and not need an engineer to tell you what a stack trace says. We're Django on the back, React/Next on the front. QA is yours end to end including release sign-off, people tend to underestimate that bit. And you're already using Claude Code or similar daily, not "open to it".
Process is screen with me, a take-home that runs about 75 mins, technical round with one of our senior PMs, then a call with our Director of Product (who you'd report to). I usually come back to people within 2 business days.
Our job board forces us to list specific countries but we hire from anywhere as long as you can do EST hours, so apply even if yours isn't on there.

jobs.title: 1st Product Manager
jobs.desc:
The company

Ooak Data turns company data into training data for AI agents.

Frontier labs can train models to reason. They cannot train them to work: navigating a real company's Slack threads, half-finished Notion docs, contradictory Jira tickets, and permission boundaries. That requires real enterprise data, and you cannot synthesize it. You have to source it.

We plug into enterprise tools, anonymize everything into a structurally identical digital twin, and generate reinforcement-learning environments with expert-level tasks calibrated against frontier models.

We are a Y Combinator company with 7 figures signed contracts with three frontier AI labs, and we are scaling delivery aggressively over the next twelve months. Three founders, full-time since December 2025: Pierre-Louis (CEO, ex-COO in edtech, sold data to frontier labs), Grégoire (CPO, first PM & head of Ops at Epsor through Series B), Thomas (CTO, ex-Head of Data at PayLead, ex-Samsung AI lab).

Why this role exists

Our engineering team ships faster than founders can specify. We have four product surfaces, most of them internal, all of them technical, and every one of them decides whether an environment ships this week or next.

We are hiring our first Product Manager to own the product: what gets built, in what order, and whether it actually made us faster.

What you will own

The full chain, from the moment a CEO agrees to share their data to the moment a frontier lab receives an environment.

Partner experience

  • The Data Hub, onboarding and export tutorials a CEO sees when they hand us their company's history. Trust and speed at the top of the funnel.

The data pipeline

  • Connectors, ingestion and anonymisation. How raw Slack, Drive, mail and CRM exports become a clean digital twin. You will spend a lot of time with Thomas (CTO) here.

Pharos, our delivery platform

  • The internal tool our Ops team lives in to run QA and delivery. Throughput is the metric. This is where 3 env a week becomes 10.

RL environments

  • The thing the labs buy. Task design, calibration, what separates a dataset from a real agent training ground.

You will run two kinds of work at once: short projects that need tight coordination across Tech, Ops and GTM this week, and long ones where nothing exists yet and you get to decide what should.

Who you are

  • A doer. You know the product methodologies and you use them when they help, not by the book. Your instinct when something is slow is to fix it, not to schedule a workshop about it.
  • AI-pilled. You vibe code. You prototype before you write a spec. You design your own mockups. You are curious about how the models themselves are built and trained.
  • UX taste, ROI brain. Our workflows have to be brutally efficient. You judge a piece of software or a workflow by efficient it allows us to be or what value it brings to our customers.
  • You keep pace. Our engineers ship a lot. You turn that into something coherent rather than slowing it down.
  • 7+ years in product, at least some of it technical: data, infra, ML, developer tools or ops platforms. Founders and first PMs who built the function from nothing are very welcome.
  • Fluent French and English. Our customers are American, our data partners spread worldwide, our team speaks both.
  • Based in Paris.

The extra that make the difference

  • A research streak: you read papers, you have opinions on RL, you have trained or fine-tuned something.

Terms

  • Compensation: €70-90k + bonus, and 0.2% to 0.5%

Pasito is the AI workspace for employee benefits.

We’re rethinking how group insurance and benefits are underwritten, delivered, used and measured - by the people who design them and the people who depend on them. We don’t build for brokers, carriers and employers - we build with them. That collaboration shows up in everything we ship: AI agents that extract and structure plan data, tools that turn complexity into clarity for employees, and workflows that save carriers and consultants hundreds of hours per case.

Today, Pasito supports many of the largest insurance carriers and brokers in the U.S. We’re backed by Y Combinator and Core Innovation Capital, and we’re growing quickly. We ship fast, iterate relentlessly, and care deeply about building systems that are accurate, scalable, and human.

jobs.title: Propulsion Product Owner
jobs.desc:
**The role**

Allocortech does not need a backlog janitor. We need someone who understands why four-quadrant FOC, voltage class, SWaP-C, and certification timeline are the product — and can turn that into a roadmap OEMs will buy.

Taurus motor controllers, Clio power/comms hubs, and the surrounding battery/PDU work already power eVTOL, hybrid cargo aircraft, and electric hydrofoils. Your job is to productize that stack.

**What you will do**

* Own the propulsion backlog: Taurus variants, voltage/power SKUs, firmware feature flags, packaging, accessories.
* Sit with EE, FOC firmware, and customers and turn “400 V, regen, eight-week MOTS” into sequenced work.
* Write requirements hardware and firmware can actually build. Kill nice-to-haves that blow SWaP or schedule.
* Partner with sales on positioning, spec sheets, and which custom asks become catalog.
* Keep the 18-month versus 24-month product bets honest.

  

**What you bring**

* 5+ years owning a technical product on power electronics, motor drives, avionics, or vehicle propulsion.
* Enough EE/firmware literacy to argue current loops, isolation, and CAN without hiding behind Jira.
* Comfort in front of aerospace, defense, or advanced-vehicle OEMs.
* Judgment on COTS vs. MOTS vs. custom — and the discipline to say no.
* Bonus: eVTOL/UAS, hybrid-electric, or maritime electric programs.

  

**Why Allocortech**

Fifty-plus people, revenue already tripled, and a propulsion line that is on vehicles instead of slides. You will set what gets built next — not write tickets for a platform team in another time zone.

***APPLY NOW***

  

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production and lab areas.

  

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package. Employees may receive equity opportunities and/or cash bonus, and have access to a robust benefits package including: top tier medical HMO, PPO & a 100% company-sponsored HSA plan option, dental and vision coverage, unlimited PTO, 11 paid holidays per year, flexible spending and dependent care savings accounts, paid parental leave, disability insurance, life insurance, and access to a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status; please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion.

**At Obie, we don’t just insure properties — we ensure progress.** With advanced technology, real-time data, and a vast network of agents and partners, we help real estate investors and landlords get insurance coverage whenever and wherever they need it. Thousands of owners nationwide trust us to be the insurance experts, so they don’t have to be.

Joining our team means embracing a fast-moving environment driven by innovation, collaboration, and constant progress. We learn quickly, iterate often, and celebrate wins together. If you're passionate about driving change and eager to impact the real estate and insurance market, Obie is the place for you.

Our Chicago based employees are hybrid, and expected to be in office on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

**Brief Summary of Role**

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Product Manager who loves figuring out how things work and can’t wait to make them better. You’ll join our growing team as an individual contributor, turning messy, technically complex problems into solutions and products that people actually use - and checking that they made a difference! You don’t need prior insurance experience; curiosity, ownership, and strong product judgement matter most.

You’ll own a meaningful product area end-to-end: bring your own point of view, get clear on why it matters to customers and the business, and build it with Design and Engineering. You enjoy turning “could we…?” into a working first version. You’ll think across customers, agents, internal teams, and interconnected systems. Initial ownership is open, with room to contribute access domains as priorities evolve.

You’re the person who asks, “What does the data say?” and then goes looking, talking to customers and teammates along the way. You can explain tradeoffs, make timely decisions with incomplete information, and follow through on results after launch. You’re curious beyond the current tools and playbook. You can point to work you’ve owned through multiple iterations and explain what changed as you learned.
* **You’re the best listener in the room:** Seek out customer insight, relevant data, and cross-functional input without treating every request as a requirement. Weigh options, make tradeoffs visible, and explain both what you recommend and what you choose not to do. You know which decisions need a deeper dive and which need a sensible call so the team can keep building.

Bring people into decisions early, navigate disagreement, and create clarity that helps others execute with confidence. The crushing weight of debt is something that we believe holds people back from reaching their dreams and making a splash in the world. So in 2013, after seeing our friends and family struggle with student loans, we created Splash Financial.

Over the years, our mission has expanded to include helping people with other forms of debt - such as refinancing credit cards, which are at all time highs in the US. And we've been able to refinance $6+ Billion in loans through our network of Splash, powered credit union and bank partners who leverage our marketplace and automated loan processing technology. And we've raised over $135 million from investors like partners of DST Global, Citi Ventures, TruStage Ventures, Northwestern Mutual Future Ventures, Detroit Venture Partners, and more.

But at our core, we're still that little company from Cleveland with a big dream: to make people more powerful than their debt and we're just getting started..

### **ABOUT OUR WORKPLACE:**

Splash is remote-first, and proud of it — though our collections team works in-person at our Arizona location.

We spend our days simplifying financial products and getting them into the hands of people who need them most. Right now, we're focused on building financial technologies that fundamentally transform how the industry lends.

Although Splash has been around since 2013, we still operate like a startup — fast-paced, nimble, and full of heart. We're good people who care deeply about doing meaningful work and we approach challenges with creativity, passion, and urgency.

And to hire the best, we provide the best: great health insurance, competitive salaries, and unique benefits like quarterly meet-ups and access to engagement tools that keep us connected — even from afar.

These values show up in how we work and how we connect — whether we're collaborating on big projects or bonding over everyday moments. Yes, we even have Slack channels for #kids-and-pets and #food because we believe being human makes us better teammates.

ABOUT REPAY
  
REPAY (“Realtime Electronic Payments” / NASDAQ TICKER: RPAY) is an established and fast-growing publicly traded financial technology and payment processing company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with offices across the country. REPAY enables its customers to accept payments anytime, anywhere, and through any channel while providing a secure, seamless, and enjoyable payment experience for the end consumers. REPAY offers a comprehensive suite of electronic payment and funding solutions, including debit and credit card processing, ACH processing, Instant Funding, and electronic bill payment systems with full IVR, text, and mobile capabilities. The scalability of its products allows merchants of all sizes to add an instant arsenal of intelligent payment technology solutions to their businesses without significant development costs or infrastructure investments.

We're seeking a Product Owner – Payment Services to help build company-wide, enterprise-level payment services for all our clients. In this role, you will blend technical and product experience in order to build enterprise-level services. You'll influence the roadmap both strategically and tactically, focusing on revenue expansion and optimization for the transaction processing product line — work that's critical to REPAY's continued growth. You'll provide leadership for service initiatives from use case identification through requirements definition and post-launch support, and play an integral part on a team with high visibility and responsibility within the organization.

* Engage with key clients on product roadmap delivery
* Turning roadmap epics into actionable work for REPAY Technology development teams in a highly professional, collaborative manner.
* Collaborating with Technology to ensure continuous investment in architecture that advances REPAY as a market leader.
* Partnering with REPAY Marketing and Technical Writers to develop product documentation, including client training materials and release notes.
* Maintaining and growing industry knowledge of card, digital wallet, and real-time payment methods across REPAY’s supported verticals
* Evangelizing REPAY’s product line and services across the company.

* Strong understanding of all aspects of Agile product development and delivery

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.desc:
Rapidly growing software company in San Fernando, CA (over 22,562 companies use our GPS tracking software) is looking to add a Product Manager to our team.

Product management is a newer function at our company. Until recently it was handled part-time across engineering, operations, and leadership, and it has outgrown that arrangement. The scope and workflows of the role are still being defined, and you'll have a hand in defining them.

We need someone who can take a project from "we should build this" all the way to "customers are using it and understand it": talking to the right people, getting the requirements right before engineering starts building, and seeing it through to launch.

If helping shape a role rather than stepping into a fully mapped-out one sounds exciting, keep reading. If you'd rather join an established product org with a playbook already written, this probably isn't the role for you.

**What You'll Own**

Every project you take on, you own end to end:

* Discovery and requirements. Sit with support, sales, operations, and customers directly. Understand the real-world task the customer is trying to complete, break it into steps, and turn those steps into features and functional requirements. Produce wireframes that show how the workflow will look on screen.
* Tickets engineering can actually build from. Write well-formed Jira tickets with clear acceptance criteria and data requirements: what's displayed live in the UI, and what needs to be stored for later reporting.
* Keeping projects moving. Coordinate with engineering leadership, design, and operations to determine where each ticket fits in overall priorities. Work with engineers on estimates, own the project timeline, make scope trade-offs to hit dates, and surface risks and slips early rather than late. Monitor tickets so nothing sits waiting for a decision that nobody knows they need to make.
* UX quality. Make sure the user can complete the task in the order they naturally think about it, and that information on screen is clear and legible.
* Testing before and after release. Test on staging and production. Find the bugs, the lag, the rough edges, and document exactly what needs to change. Retest until it feels production-ready.
* Internal rollout and training. Write up how each release works, train internal staff, and be the go-to person for questions. Coordinate staff testing of new features and channel that feedback back to engineering.
* Launch. Draft customer-facing announcements and coordinate final release timing with the development team.

Discovery, requirements, and keeping projects moving are the core of the job. Testing, internal training, and launch communications are also part of it, because on a small team the person who owns a feature sees it all the way through; if those parts sound like a chore rather than part of shipping well, please don't apply.

**The Technical Bar**

You don't need to write code. You do need to be able to hold a productive conversation with an engineer about what's possible, what's hard, and what the trade-offs are, and you need to understand why something that sounds like a simple feature may actually be difficult. You should be comfortable looking at how the application behaves and at its data model well enough to specify what should be shown on screen versus stored for reporting.

Our product is GPS fleet tracking, which means physical devices in vehicles, firmware, cellular connectivity, and a lot of data arriving in near real time. Prior experience with a product that includes hardware or devices is a real plus.

Our stack, for context: Golang and MySQL on the server, Vue.js on the web, Swift (iOS) and Kotlin (Android) for mobile, on AWS.

**Ramp-up and the 60-day review**

Nobody expects you to know our system on day one. Your first weeks will be spent learning the product alongside support and operations before you take ownership of a project.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.desc:
**About Clair**
---------------

If you can send your friends money in seconds, why does it still take your employer two weeks to send your paycheck?

At Clair, we are on a mission to create financial freedom for America's workers by giving them a digital banking platform that allows them to get paid as soon as they clock out of work. But we're not just another digital bank or on-demand pay provider. We meet Americans at their place of work by embedding our products within the scheduling, workforce management, and payroll apps they already use every day.

Learn more about us at getclair.com/about

**About the Role**
------------------

We’re looking for a Product Manager to help bring one of Clair's next products to life.

The product you'll initially work on exists today in successful private beta and is actively being expanded. That means you'll have a unique opportunity to join early in the product journey and help shape how we take an idea from concept to a real-world product and experience.

This isn't a role where you'll inherit a perfectly defined roadmap or be handed a clear playbook for success. We have a direction, a problem we're working to solve, and a vision, but there is still plenty to figure out. You'll help turn ambiguity into action, make smart decisions with imperfect information, and work alongside a small, highly collaborative team to build, test, learn, and iterate quickly.

At Clair, building products is uniquely complex. We're an embedded fintech company, which means great product decisions require balancing the needs of our users with partner priorities and internal business demands, all while operating within a regulated environment. You'll work closely with engineering, design, data, finance, regulatory, operations, go-to-market, and partner teams to navigate those competing inputs and find the best path forward.

We're looking for a builder who is comfortable with gray areas, thinks outside the box, and isn't afraid to try something that might not work. You know how to move quickly without being reckless and understand that failing fast is only valuable if you're learning fast, too.

You won't be joining a team with every answer already mapped out. You'll help us find them.

**If you need someone to tell you exactly how to win, this probably isn't the role for you.**

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Identify, evaluate, and help define opportunities for new Clair products and experiences, often before the problem or solution is fully understood.
* Define and execute product strategy and roadmaps in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
* Partner closely with engineering and design to move quickly from concept to experiment to product, balancing speed with thoughtful execution.
* Build, test, learn, and iterate quickly—knowing when to invest further and when to fail fast and move on.
* Balance user experience and needs with partner priorities, business requirements, and the realities of operating an embedded fintech product.
* Spend time with partner management and go-to-market teams to identify new opportunities, uncover unmet needs, and develop new product concepts when necessary.
* Develop a deep understanding of Clair users through feedback, behavioral data, research, and direct conversations—and push for new ways to learn when existing data isn't enough.
* Work closely with data and analytics teams to develop hypotheses, evaluate product performance, and make informed decisions without becoming paralyzed by incomplete data.
* Collaborate with design and support teams to create intuitive, elegant experiences that help users understand and confidently engage with financial products.
* Partner with regulatory, finance, operations, and other internal stakeholders to navigate complex requirements without losing sight of the user experience.
* Bring the voice of the customer into product strategy, roadmap discussions, and day-to-day product decisions.

Across **Slots, Card & Table, and Arcade games**, we are creating differentiated experiences that combine proven player appeal, outstanding creative execution, innovative mechanics, and the quality expected from the Hard Rock brand. You’ll have the opportunity to help shape these games from the ground up, working across our internal team and external development partners to create content that can become a meaningful part of our casino portfolio and player experience.

**What’s the position?**

We’re looking for a **Product Manager / Game Producer, Casino Games** to help build the next generation of proprietary games for Hard Rock Bet Casino. This is a high impact role combining **Product Management, Game Production, Game Design,** and commercial product thinking. Depending on Studio priorities and individual experience, you may lead games across Slots, Card & Table, Arcade, or multiple categories.

You will own games from the first concept through development, certification, launch, and performance review. Working closely with the Senior Director, Studio leadership, internal stakeholders, RGS and platform partners, and external game development studios, you will turn player and market insights into high-quality games that drive engagement, differentiation, and revenue. The role requires someone equally comfortable discussing game mechanics and player experience with creatives, math and requirements with development teams, delivery with external studios, product strategy and performance with senior stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Own the Full Game Lifecycle**: Lead casino games from concept and business case through game design, development, QA, certification, launch, and post launch performance.
* **Build and Drive the Roadmap**: Develop and manage a strong game roadmap across Slots, Card & Table, and Arcade based on player needs, market opportunities, business priorities, and portfolio gaps.
* **Act as Product Manager and Game Producer**: Translate strategy into clear game concepts, GDDs, requirements, priorities, milestones, and actionable development plans.
* **Champion Creative and Game Quality**: Guide gameplay, mechanics, math, features, art, animation, audio, UI/UX, and overall player experience to deliver polished, compelling games.
* **Drive Innovation with Purpose**: Analyze successful games, suppliers, mechanics, player behavior, and adjacent gaming categories to identify opportunities worth adapting, improving, or reinventing.
* **Lead Internal and External Development**: Work closely with external studios, RGS and platform partners, Product, Engineering, Art, Math, QA, Compliance, Release, Analytics, Marketing, and Casino Operations to deliver games successfully.
* **Manage Delivery and Risk**: Own game priorities, development milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and stakeholder communication while maintaining quality and speed to market.
* **Deliver for Regulated Markets**: Ensure game design, math, functionality, documentation, testing, and implementation meet applicable regulatory and certification requirements.

jobs.title: Product Owner, Manufacturing Vision & Quality Systems
jobs.desc:
When you join the Sandalwood team, you’ll join an engaging and inclusive group with a mission to help our customers identify, assess, and reduce work-related risks to quality, productivity, and employee health.

We are seeking a passionate support associate to lead the functional definition, lifecycle development, plant integration, and operational rollout of next-generation computer vision and automated inspection solutions.

In this role, you will own and advance a portfolio may include multiple advanced vision integration projects. You will work at the intersection of manufacturing, quality, software engineering, machine learning, controls, and plant operations to turn complex production challenges into scalable digital products.

Your success will help manufacturing teams improve first-time-through quality, reduce scrap, strengthen defect containment, and prevent quality issues from reaching customers.

This is an opportunity to shape products that directly influence manufacturing quality, production performance, and customer protection. You will have meaningful ownership of the roadmap while working closely with the teams that design, deploy, operate, and depend on these systems every day.

**What You'll Do**

Own the Product Backlog and Roadmap

* Define, prioritize, and manage the product backlog for camera and sensor based solutions.
* Align roadmap priorities with plant quality objectives and the broader digital manufacturing strategy.
* Translate manufacturing requirements, business needs, and quality risks into actionable user stories, acceptance criteria, and product increments.

Partner with Manufacturing Stakeholders

* Collaborate with Assembly, Stamping, and Powertrain teams to understand inspection challenges and operational requirements.
* Engage plant-floor technicians, quality leaders, controls engineers, plant management, software developers, and system integrators.
* Define functional specifications for applications such as visual defect detection and part presence or absence verification.

Lead Agile Product Delivery

* Serve as the primary product authority throughout the Agile delivery lifecycle.
* Lead or actively participate in sprint planning, daily stand-ups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
* Provide direction and timely decisions to software engineers, machine learning engineers, and system integration teams.
* Keep delivery teams focused on the features and capabilities that create the greatest manufacturing and quality value.

Define Quality and Performance Criteria

* Establish clear acceptance criteria and quality-gating logic for automated inspection applications.
* Define false-positive and false-negative thresholds based on manufacturing requirements.
* Support inspection strategies for applications and critical vehicle build verification.

Guide Deployment and Production Validation

* Lead User Acceptance Testing, line-side validation, commissioning runs, and run-at-rate trials.
* Coordinate with plant and technical teams to verify that solutions are ready for production deployment.
* Support manufacturing launches and help resolve deployment issues in plant-floor environments.

Measure Results and Drive Continuous Improvement

* Establish, monitor, and communicate key performance indicators, including:
* First-time-through quality
* False rejection rate
* Inspection accuracy
* Cycle-time impact
* System uptime
* Mean time to detect and resolve issues
* Communicate product performance and improvement opportunities to plant and executive leadership.
* Use operating data and stakeholder feedback to continually improve product capabilities and deployment standards.

Enable Adoption and Operational Readiness

* Champion change management and product adoption across manufacturing operations.
* Support the creation of standard operating procedures and operational documentation.
Coordinate training for line operators, plant quality leads, and controls technicians.

At the center of our platform are AI agents that do real work for our customers: agents that carry multi-step, high-stakes workflows through to completion, with real money and real relationships on the line. We're looking for a PM to own these agentic experiences. There's no established playbook for this work; the patterns for running agents in production are being figured out in real time, by a small number of teams, and we're one of the teams doing the inventing. You'll own how our agents behave, how their quality is measured and improved, and how the system earns the trust to take on more. AI isn't a feature we bolted on, it's the foundation of our product and how we run the company: we automate what can be automated so people spend their time on judgment, not busywork. As a PM here, you'll prototype ideas yourself, get answers from data without waiting on anyone, and ship faster than you're probably used to.

==========================

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. ============

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company supplying the minerals critical to modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. Our data systems don't live in a vacuum — they feed process simulators, drive site automation, and are the substrate the business runs its decisions on.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to be the single product owner for the data engineering family — the data platform, analytics, data science, and the AI and agentic workflows built on top of them. Today this work is spread across technical leads and absorbed informally, with no one setting direction across the whole. Your job is to change that: decide what the data organization builds and why, get stakeholders aligned behind it, and make sure engineers can stay heads-down on the work that matters.

This is a hybrid Pioneer/Settler role: you'll get lightweight demos and PoCs built on ambiguous problems, and you'll bring order and cohesive ownership to data work streams that already exist. You'll prioritize ruthlessly and visibly — being explicit about what will not be worked on — and set direction rather than waiting for it to be handed to you.

* Set the bar for what "supported" and "correct" mean as tools graduate from scripts and spreadsheets, and be explicit about what won't be migrated.

jobs.desc:
**About the role:**

LSEG Analytics has been trusted for over 30 years by portfolio managers, risk teams and quantitative analysts. These clients want to access analytics where they're already working. This happens in spreadsheets, notebooks, BI dashboards, automated workflows and increasingly in AI assistants and agents.

Every one of those interactions is evidence: what customers actually use, how often, through which surface, and whether it worked. Today that evidence is uneven, which means the teams who build, sell and support our analytics have an incomplete picture of how customers experience them. This role owns closing that gap.

You will lead telemetry strategy across our analytics platform, owning what gets captured at the point of use, what it means, how it is surfaced, and working with the central telemetry team to ensure that the reporting is meaningful and consistent with D&A standards. That spans instrumentation standards, product adoption analytics, the usage evidence that supports commercial decisions, and the reporting our product, commercial and client service teams rely on.

This is a horizontal role. Telemetry cuts across every analytics vertical and every delivery channel, which means broad exposure to the LSEG estate and to the teams behind it.

This is a hands-on role. You will run your own discovery, own your roadmap, work directly with engineering to deliver, and stay accountable for the success of what you ship.

  

**Responsibilities:**

* Own the strategy and roadmap for analytics product telemetry, from instrumentation at the gateway through to the reporting and visualization built on top of it
* Collaborate with product teams to define what gets captured and what it means: the event schema, the identity and entitlement dimensions, and the rules that make usage comparable and actionable across products surfaces
* Partner with the cloud data platform teams who own storage and pipeline, translating product requirements into what the platform needs to capture and retain
* Inform the consumption layer: dashboards, usage reporting and the visualizations that make customer behaviour legible to the teams who act on it
* Turn usage data into an account of the customer experience — where workflows succeed, where they stall, and which surfaces customers are actually choosing
* Run discovery with your internal consumers across product, commercial, client service and engineering, and treat them as customers of what you build
* Hold the line on data quality and consistency, and be the person who can say what a number means and where it came from
* Act as the subject matter expert on usage data for commercial, client service and internal stakeholders
* Track how consumption patterns are changing, particularly agentic and AI-assisted usage, and make sure measurement keeps pace with them
  

**Background Experience/Skills:**

* Product management experience, or an equivalent background owning a platform, data or API product for internal or external consumers
* Technical fluency: comfortable with APIs, event data and data structures, and able to hold a credible conversation with engineers. You don't need to write production code, but you should be able to read it and be competent with SQL
* A feel for how data gets presented: you can tell the difference between a dashboard people open once and one they use to make decisions
* Data-driven in practice, not just in principle: you define what success looks like before you build, instrument for it, and change course when the evidence says to
* Judgment about measurement itself: you know the difference between a metric that is easy to collect and one that is worth acting on
* Working familiarity with AI tooling and how agentic consumption differs from human consumption
* Experience in financial data and analytics
* Comfortable operating in a matrixed organization
* Degree or equivalent in: Bachelors Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering/Operations Research

Description:

At CSpring, we believe in the power of data to drive decisions and real-world impact. We’re a purpose-driven consulting firm specializing in data strategy, data engineering, and data analytics. Our clients span the public and private sectors, and our work helps them solve complex problems, gain insights, and achieve measurable results.

We're seeking talented professionals who are collaborative, curious, and committed to making a difference that thrive at the intersection of data, technology, and business strategy. Whether you're passionate about transforming public programs, enabling executive decision-making, or modernizing legacy systems, you'll find meaningful work and purpose here.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here**

* **Purposeful Projects** – Improve systems that serve real people by delivering smarter data, streamlined processes, and strategic insight.
* **People-First Culture** – We’re as committed to your growth as we are to delivering high-impact solutions. You’ll find support, autonomy, and community here.
* **Strategic, Hands-On Work** – From data architecture and documentation to client workshops and solution delivery, you’ll influence every step of the process.
* **Collaborative Trust** – Our clients rely on us to listen carefully, deliver consistently, and guide wisely. We partner with integrity, curiosity, and heart.

**What You'll Do**

You'll work with clients to turn their enterprise data vision into a defined, sequenced, and communicated plan of record:

* Own product definition for the data portfolio — reporting and analytics, privacy-by-design, segmentation, predictive models, and the platform capabilities underneath them.
* Maintain the roadmap: a rolling view of what the data team is delivering across the next two to three quarters, kept current, and defensible to any executive who asks why something sits where it does.
* Write the product vision documents, acceptance criteria, and release notes that let engineers build without guessing and let stakeholders know what they are getting.
* Define what success looks like for every product, instrument it, and report on it — usage, adoption by department, time to insight, model performance in production, and the business result it was built to move.
* Say plainly when something isn't working, and change or retire products that don't earn their usage.
* Run the planning and execution rhythm: monthly planning, standups, and the working agreements that keep a small senior team moving on a Kanban flow.
* Keep BAU visible and bounded so it doesn't quietly consume delivery capacity.
* Sit with every function that touches fan, revenue, or venue data, understand what each is trying to accomplish, translate that into data product requirements, and close the loop when something ships.
* Serve as the standing connection between the data team and the rest of the organization.
* Write status that executives can read in one pass, launch communications that drive adoption, and documentation that makes the portfolio legible to people who weren't in the room.

Requirements:

* Seven or more years in product management, with meaningful time on data, analytics, or platform products.
* Experience with a modern data stack, enough to hold a credible conversation with engineers about tradeoffs without needing to write the code.
* Demonstrated ability to run planning and delivery for a technical team, and a track record of setting and reporting on product metrics rather than tracking output.
* Strong written communication, specifically the ability to write for executives.
* Working fluency with AI tooling in daily practice.
* A track record of taking data products from vision to adoption.

**Bonus Experience**

* Sports, entertainment, media, or consumer businesses with large customer bases.
* Defining AI-enabled product capabilities — conversational access to data, agent-driven insight delivery, or models embedded in business workflow.
* Privacy-by-design or data gove

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.desc:
Zlayt AI is a litigation automation platform built exclusively for personal injury law. From demand letters and deposition summaries to discovery responses and case analysis, Zlayt equips law firms with intelligent tools that draft faster, think strategically, and deliver results without friction, setup, or compromise.

We're an early-stage, product-led company building the category-defining product for legal AI in a large, underserved niche. This is a rare opportunity to shape what the product becomes — working directly with the founding team, real PI lawyers, and real case data.

**The Role**

Zlayt AI is hiring a Product Manager to own the product from problem to shipped feature. You'll work directly with the founders and engineering to decide what we build, why, and in what order — then make sure it ships and actually works for the lawyers and legal assistants who use it every day.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's role. There is no product org to step into. You'll be writing the first specs, running the first structured discovery, and setting up how product decisions get made.

**What You'll Do**

* Own the product roadmap: talk to PI lawyers and staff, find the highest-value workflow problems, and turn them into a prioritized plan
* Write clear specs and acceptance criteria that engineers can build from without guesswork
* Work hands-on with AI: define how features should behave, test outputs against real legal work product, and set the quality bar for what "good enough to ship" means
* Run discovery and feedback loops with early customers, including Zinda Law Group as the first major client
* Define and track the metrics that show whether a feature is working (adoption, time saved, output quality, retention)
* Operate with significant ambiguity in an early-stage environment, making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting quickly

  

**Who You Are**

* **A builder, not an inheritor:** You've shipped a 0-to-1 software product or major feature as the accountable PM — you know what it takes to build something from nothing, not just run an existing roadmap
* **Technical enough to be dangerous:** You've worked directly with engineers day to day, can read a technical design, and don't need a translator to discuss APIs, data models, or model behavior
* **AI-native:** You've shipped or worked hands-on with LLM or AI-powered features, and you use AI tools yourself to do your own work faster
* **Workflow-obsessed:** You've built software for a demanding professional user — legal, healthcare, finance, or similar — where the details of the workflow decide whether the product gets used
* **Startup-tested:** You've worked in small, fast-moving companies where you had to build process yourself, not step into one that already existed
* **Self-directed:** Your track record shows work you personally drove — not just team results you were adjacent to
* **Experienced but still hands-on:** Roughly 4–10 years of total professional experience, with at least 3 in product management
* **Stable but not stagnant:** A track record of meaningful tenure at each stop, with job changes that make sense (promotions, acquisitions, layoffs, or clear career logic — not a pattern of short stints)

  

**Our Philosophy**

We firmly uphold the value of every individual within our team, ensuring they have the chance to build a rewarding career both financially and personally. Our firm's structure is designed to offer exceptional prospects for growth and advancement. At Zlayt AI, every team member leaves at the end of the day with the satisfaction of knowing they have diligently served our clients and positively impacted the lives of others. Join us and experience a remarkable work environment at our organization!
